## [2026-08-06] — CI guard: agent/tool documentation drift now fails the build

### Added
- **`scripts/check_agent_doc_drift.py`** — stdlib-only guard that treats the code as the source
  of truth for the agent roster and the tool registry. Three checks:
  1. `app/tools/registry.py`'s module docstring count == `len(BUILTIN_TOOLS)`.
  2. Every `"N specialist agents"` claim in `.claude/rules/agents.md` == the number of specialist
     agents in code.
  3. Every specialist's display name actually appears in `agents.md` — a count alone would pass if
     someone added an agent and bumped the number without adding the roster row.
- **`agent-doc-drift` job in `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml`**, wired into the `summary`
  job's `needs` + aggregation loop so a failure actually blocks the merge. A guard that reports
  but does not gate is theatre.

### Why
The 2026-08-06 inventory found three drifts that had accumulated silently — the registry docstring
said "6 MCP tools" against 9 registered, and `agents.md` said "17 specialist agents" against 19,
with **Summit and Chronicle both** missing from the roster. Every one was a one-line edit somebody
forgot. Nothing failed, so nothing surfaced them.

The job is deliberately **ungated** — no `if:`, no path filter. It is pure stdlib and runs in ~1s,
and gating on "did you touch agents/ or tools/" is exactly how the drift got in: the roster rots
when somebody edits an orchestrator, not only when they edit the doc. Always-run also sidesteps
the trap already called out in `detect-changes` — a PR that only edits a guard must still exercise
the guard it ships.

### Fixed — the inventory document was not actually reproducible
`scripts/build_ig_agent_tool_inventory.py` is a *renderer*: it consumes `--agents` / `--tools`
JSON. The AST extractor that produced that JSON was never committed, so the changelog claim that
the document "regenerates in one command" was false — from a clean checkout it could not be
regenerated at all. The same extraction the guard needs now lives in the committed script, so:

```
python3 scripts/check_agent_doc_drift.py --emit-agents /tmp/a.json --emit-tools /tmp/t.json
python3 scripts/build_ig_agent_tool_inventory.py --agents /tmp/a.json --tools /tmp/t.json \
    --out IG_Agent_and_Tool_Inventory.docx --logo Logo-Dark.png
```
Verified the committed extractor reproduces the exact JSON behind the shipped document (22 agent
classes, 9 built-in tools, 50 pack modules — identical), and the round trip rebuilds the .docx.

### Changed
- **`.claude/rules/agents.md`** — note under the roster stating the counts are CI-enforced and
  what to run locally. Phrased to avoid introducing a new `"N specialist agents"` claim the guard
  would then have to police.

### Verification
- Passes on `development` (19 specialists, 9 built-in tools).
- **Five negative tests, each confirmed to fail the guard:** stale docstring count; a 10th tool
  added without bumping the docstring; a new agent with `agents.md` untouched; the subtle case
  where the count is bumped but the roster row is still missing; and — the real regression proof —
  running the guard against `development` as it stood *before* the fix (`751891a9`), where it
  correctly reports all three historical drifts including both missing agents.
- Workflow YAML parsed and asserted: job present, ungated, in `summary.needs`, in the env block,
  and in the aggregation loop. A typo in any of those would make a failing guard silently pass.
- Observed drift in the wild: three functions (`behaviour_scores`, `extract_evidence`,
  `prism_dimension_detail`) landed in `lumen/self_portrait.py` between the document being
  generated and this entry — one day.

## [2026-08-05] — ts-jest was failing to emit a test file, blocking deploys

Not a flake, and not cheap: the shared TypeScript program cost ~22 minutes of CI
per run AND intermittently failed to compile a file. PR #371 (merge `0a0d7b46`).

### The symptom
`src/hooks/interview/__tests__/useSpeechDictation.test.tsx` failed to RUN, never
to assert — every occurrence read `4363 tests passed, 1 suite failed`:

```
Unable to process '<file>', please make sure that `outDir` in your tsconfig is
neither '' or '.'
```

Four times on 2026-08-05 across unrelated branches (#365's first run, #366's
development run, #369's first run, #370's). On #370 it turned deterministic:
**three consecutive reruns of the same commit all failed**, skipping Deploy to
Dev and Deploy to Staging-B each time and leaving the HomeV2 rework undeployable
for over an hour.

### Cause, read from ts-jest 29.4 rather than inferred
```
ts-compiler.js:74   if (!this.configSet.isolatedModules) { …language service… }
ts-compiler.js:193  if (output.emitSkipped) throw Errors.CannotProcessFile
ts-compiler.js:238  return this._ts.transpileModule(…)
```
The throw is reachable only on the LanguageService path, guarded by exactly that
flag. `"isolatedModules": true` in `tsconfig.test.json` makes ts-jest transpile
each file on its own, which cannot reach it.

### Why this costs no type safety
`jest.config.ts` already sets `diagnostics.warnOnly: true` with TS1343/TS2339
ignored — **jest was never a type gate**. It was paying for a type-aware program
and deriving nothing from it. Real type-checking is `npm run build` (tsc) as its
own CI job; `tsconfig.test.json` is test-only, so that build is untouched
(verified). The flag goes in the tsconfig, not the ts-jest transform options:
the transform-level form is deprecated in 29.x.

### Result
**Unit Tests 25 min → 2m47s on the same runner**, and green. Same 550 suites.

- Files: `inspire-genius-frontend/tsconfig.test.json`

### The verification gap that made this take four rounds
`npm run test:ci` is bare `jest` — **no `--coverage`**. CI runs
`npx jest --ci --forceExit --coverage --coverageThreshold=…`. Every "550/550
green" reported earlier in the session therefore never exercised the failing
path, while being described as the identical CI command. Re-verified since with
the real invocation: 550 suites / 4365 tests.

### Risk accepted
`isolatedModules` forbids `const enum` and type-only re-exports without
`export type`. Confirmed no `const enum` in `src/`; full suite passes.

## [2026-08-05] — HomeV2 reworked: last-visit lead, Today's Prep tile, fewer shortcuts

Seven changes to the Home page, all on request. Frontend-only; PR #370
(merge `10b7559`).

### Removed
- **The Chat-with-Meridian tile.** WelcomeBackTile moves up into its place, so
  "move the 2nd tile to the top" falls out of the removal. Meridian is still one
  click away in the sidebar.
- **"Other Assessments"** (DISC / MBTI / Clifton / Hogan / Big Five), with its
  now-unreachable Add-assessment modal and the `loaded-frameworks` read whose
  only consumer it was. Those results are still addable from the Documents
  surface — the Home shortcut went, not the capability.
  - Files: `inspire-genius-frontend/src/pages/user/HomeV2.tsx`,
    `inspire-genius-frontend/src/components/dashboard/v2/WelcomeBackTile.tsx`

### Changed
- **"Welcome back, {name}" → "Here's what you worked on last visit."** plus the
  user's recent Meridian conversations with relative times. Sourced from the
  same conversation query the chat History dropdown uses, so the two cannot
  disagree about what the recent work was. With no history it says so and offers
  "start a conversation" rather than rendering an empty list — which is
  indistinguishable from a failed fetch.
- **Videos line** added above the quick-action row that holds the Videos
  dropdown, so the copy sits beside the control it describes. Spelling corrected
  to "InspiresGenius".
- **Self-Portrait and My Journey greyed + locked.** A per-SHORTCUT lever
  (`LOCKED_QUICK_ACTIONS`), deliberately separate from the vertical-level
  `isVerticalForceDisabled`: Lumen and Direction Setting are still live products
  and stay reachable elsewhere. Both read "Temporarily unavailable" rather than
  the entitlement wording, which would be false for an entitled user.
- **Personal Info** moved to the end of the quick-action row, sized to content,
  with a floating panel — an inline expansion inside a flex row shoves that
  row's layout on every open.

### Added
- **"Today's Prep" tile** rendering the Lumen Moments surface inline. Moments
  gained an `embedded` variant dropping its page `<h1>` and padding — a variant,
  not a copy, so the tile and `/vertical/lumen/moments` cannot drift.
  - Files: `inspire-genius-frontend/src/pages/lumen/Moments.tsx`

### Fixed — a bug this change introduced, caught by the existing suite
Moving Personal Info into the quick-action row initially gated it on
`quickActions.length || videos.length`, so a user with neither lost Personal Info
entirely. The row now also renders for Personal Info alone, with a test in each
direction.

### Deliberately NOT done — no deep-link from the last-visit list
The entries open the chat but do **not** select the clicked conversation.
`MeridianChat`'s route-state contract is `prefillPrompt` / `autoSubmit` /
`prefillDisplay` only — there is no `conversationId` entry point, so passing one
would have been a silent no-op that looked like a working link in review. This
matches what the previous "Last time we discussed…" button did. Deep-linking is
a MeridianChat change, not a Home one.

### i18n — six new keys across ALL 21 locales
Real translations, not just the 10 languages the parity test checks: an `en`-only
key fails that gate, and English text in a non-English bundle is the defect the
gate exists to catch. "InspiresGenius" stays untranslated as a product name.

### Verification
Rendered the composed page and read the result rather than trusting assertions
alone: two tiles in the right order, three pills locked with the honest tooltip,
Moments' ask box mounted inside the tile with no duplicate heading.
`npm run test:ci` 550 suites / 4365 tests all passing; build and eslint clean.

**Process note:** the PR was merged with `gh pr merge --auto`, which fell back to
an immediate merge because auto-merge is not enabled on the repo — so it landed
on three of four green gates, with Unit Tests still pending, rather than four.
No practical consequence (the full suite was green locally and the deploy re-runs
it), but `--auto` is not a safe way to gate a merge on this repo.

## [2026-08-05] — Audit: PRISM survey request → completion → return pipeline

Investigation only (no code change). Confirmed the end-to-end PRISM
request/return pipeline against `origin/development` code + live dev/staging-b
probes (ECS task defs, `prism-poll-trigger` Lambda config/logs, Aurora via
`migration-runner`). Full write-up: `docs/prism/prism_request_pipeline_audit_2026-08-04.md`.

### Findings
- **Pipeline is fully built in code** (`app/prism/{client,poller,ingestor,csv_builder}.py`,
  `routes/prism_request.py`, `services/prism-poll-trigger/`) but has **never run
  end-to-end** on either env. Live DB: dev 1 / staging-b 4 `prism_requests`, ALL
  `pending`, 0 completed, **0 `api_ingest` assessments**.
- **Poller dead (both envs):** `prism-poll-trigger` fires every 30 min but errors
  every time — `AGENT_ENGINE_BASE_URL and SECRET_KEY ... required`; deployed code
  frozen 2026-06-22, stale vs development. Never calls `/v1/prism/poll/run`.
- **S3 not wired:** ingestor targets `AGENT_ENGINE_PRISM_DOCUMENTS_BUCKET` (unset
  on both agent-engines) → PDF/CSV PUT would raise → row `failed`. No PDF stored.
- **document-service registration not wired** (`DOCUMENT_SERVICE_URL`/`PRISM_ADMIN_TOKEN` unset).
- **Read-store gap:** ingestor §16 writes ONLY `assessments`/`assessment_scores`,
  never `prism_results` — but the runtime READS `prism_results` (#794). Ingested
  scores would be authoritative-but-invisible. #794 mirror runs only on admin paths.
- **PDF popup:** dedicated `PrismReportViewer` (`GET /v1/prism/report/{id}`) is dead
  code (404). The live HomeV2 "View Inventory PDF" popup shows a docgen Self-Portrait
  from `prism_results`, NOT the real PRISM PDF; no route serves `pdf_s3_key`.
- **PRISM UK portal retrieval:** `CreateUser=true` creates a PRISM-side record;
  `UnlockReport` client exists but is never called; portal-side download is a
  PRISM-UK capability we don't expose or broker.

### Answers
1. CSV is **synthesized** by us (not a literal PRISM file); scores WOULD link to the
   user in `assessments`/`assessment_scores` but (a) nothing triggers ingest, (b) S3
   unconfigured, (c) scores would be invisible. Net: not happening today.
2. **No** — user cannot view the actual PRISM PDF in a popup (dedicated viewer 404s;
   working popup shows a different, platform-generated doc).
3. Not through our platform; PRISM-portal retrieval is PRISM-UK-side and unexposed.

- Files: `docs/prism/prism_request_pipeline_audit_2026-08-04.md`

## [2026-08-05] — Activate the PRISM request → completion → return pipeline (G9 gaps #1–4 + Q3)

Remediation of the 2026-08-04 audit. A completed PRISM survey now returns scores
(visible platform-wide) + PDF/CSV (downloadable by the user). Backend PR #815,
FE PR #367. **Deployed + verified on dev + staging-b** (tag
`release-stable-2026-08-05-prism-pipeline`).

### Fixed
- **Poll-trigger signing key (gap #1 — root cause corrected).** The audit read
  the dead poll as "stale Lambda code"; verified via CloudWatch + git + `cdk diff`
  that `handler.py` is unchanged since 2026-06-21 and the twin `rollup-trigger`
  fails identically. Real cause: `voice-agent-secrets-<env>` has **no SECRET_KEY
  field**, so `_resolve_secret_key()` returned `""` and every run errored
  `AGENT_ENGINE_BASE_URL and SECRET_KEY ... required`. Added a dedicated
  CDK-generated plain-text signing secret (`ig-<env>-service-signing-key`); both
  triggers sign with it and the agent-engine verifies with it (injected
  `SECRET_KEY`). Non-breaking: magic-auth/Cognito tokens keep the
  unverified-claims fallback; only internal super-admin tokens become genuinely
  verified. Verified: poll-trigger now returns 200 (`polled` 1 dev / 4 staging-b,
  0 errors) — no more SECRET_KEY error.
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts`

### Added / Changed
- **PRISM documents bucket wired (gap #2).** `AGENT_ENGINE_PRISM_DOCUMENTS_BUCKET
  = ig-<env>-documents` on the agent-engine task def so the ingestor S3 PUT stops
  raising and the row reaches `done`. S3 PutObject/GetObject grants already
  existed (services-stack `PrismIngestorUsersPrefixWrite` / `ReadMonolithUploadBucket`).
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts`
- **Read-store bridge (gap #4).** New shared
  `services/agent-engine/app/prism/results_projection.py` mirrors an api_ingest
  assessment into `prism_results` (reusing `prism_canon.derive_colours`), used by
  BOTH the #794 admin path and the poll-ingest path — so ingested profiles are
  visible to chat / dashboards / RAG / Job-Fit. Also fixed
  `ingestor._build_synthetic_payload` to tag the 8 BehaviorPreferences behaviours
  as `(BehaviorPreferences, Underlying)` (the canonical address readers +
  `derive_colours` expect — otherwise the mirror wrote zero rows).
  - Files: `results_projection.py`, `prism/ingestor.py`, `routes/profile_admin.py`
- **User-facing PRISM report download (gap #3 + report popup).** New
  `GET /v1/prism/report/me` (availability + portal URL) and
  `GET /v1/prism/requests/{id}/report/download?kind=pdf|csv` (self-owned 5-min
  presigned S3 URLs) for the *real* PRISM PDF/CSV — distinct from the docgen
  Self-Portrait. The ingestor also registers the artifacts directly in the
  `documents` table so they surface on the Documents page. FE: "View PRISM Report
  PDF" button on the assessment page opening the existing `DocumentIframeModal`,
  plus a "Retrieve from the PRISM portal" link. Verified live: routes 401 (auth
  required) vs 404 (bogus) on both envs.
  - Files: `routes/prism_report_download.py`, `main.py`; FE
    `services/prism/prismReport.service.ts`, `hooks/prism/usePrismReportDownload.ts`,
    `pages/user/PrismAssessment.tsx`
- **UnlockReport (§5.2, Q3).** The ingestor calls `unlock_report` before fetching
  so PRISM report access is authorised and the PRISM-portal ActionURL1 is captured
  on the assessment payload and surfaced by `/report/me`.
  - Files: `prism/ingestor.py`

### Tests
- New `test_prism_report_download.py` (5), ingestor T6 mirror + idempotency, FE
  service (3) + hook (3). Updated the §16 grep test (prism_results now
  intentionally allowed via the shared projection; legacy vectorizer still

Still listed, greyed, lock-marked and non-navigating. Routes and pages are

Job Fit is **not in `getUserNavItems` at all**. It reaches My Workspace from the
vertical registry via `useWorkspaceNavItems`, where `disabled` is derived from

not reappear in the Tools rollup while switched off.

removes an entry, entitlement decides whether a visible entry is usable, and
`FORCE_DISABLED_VERTICALS` overrides entitlement to force one off.

off for **everyone**, including users whose plan does include Job Fit, so that
message would have been false. Added `NavItemDef.disabledReason`; the three read

## [2026-08-04] — Critical-gap limit 25 → 35: measured, and only a partial fix

Follow-up to the "all Poor fit" work. The guardrail was the last layer, and this
records what raising its threshold actually did rather than what it was meant to.

### What the guardrail is
Separate from the fit score, `guardrails.py` caps the tier: **≥2 critical gaps →
`misalignment`** (1 → cap at potential-fit). A *critical gap* is a dimension the
role benchmarks at **≥65** where the candidate is more than **25** points short.
The intent is sound — do not call someone a strong match when they are badly
short on two things the role cannot do without. It is why a row could read
`fitScore: 81` and `tier: misalignment` at once: both true, measuring different
things.

### Changed — the limit is now tunable, 35 on dev and staging-b
- **The rule itself is untouched.** 2+ gaps still force misalignment, 1 still
  caps at potential-fit, the cap still only moves a tier downward. A test
  asserts it explicitly, and another asserts that widening the limit does not
  widen *which* dimensions count as critical (benchmark <65 still never counts).
- `evaluate_candidate` gained `critical_gap_limit`, defaulting to the shipped
  25.0 — 135 existing scoring tests confirm the default is genuinely unchanged.
  All **five** service call sites pass it; a setting nothing reads is worse than
  no setting.
- `_critical_gap_limit()` falls back to 25.0 on anything unparseable **or
  non-positive** — a zero limit would make every dimension critical, which is
  the opposite failure and worse than a typo.
- Roll back: `-c blueprintCriticalGapLimit=25`.
- Files: `packages/ig-blueprint-scoring/ig_blueprint_scoring/guardrails.py`,
  `services/blueprint-service/app/{config,service}.py`,
  `infrastructure/cdk/lib/blueprint-service-stack.ts`

### Measured on dev — it helped, partially
|  | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `criticalGapCount` | 4×2 · 14×3 · 10×4 · 4×5 | **6×1** · 8×2 · 8×3 · 8×4 · 2×5 |
| `tier` | **32 × misalignment** | **26 misalignment · 5 potential-fit · 1 moderate-fit** |
| `displayBand` | 3 Excellent · 7 Good · 7 Moderate · 15 Poor | unchanged |

**6 of 32 roles uncapped** — the first time `tier` has discriminated at all
rather than being constant. But **26 still read misalignment**: 18 roles carry
3+ critical gaps even at 35. Predicted before deploying (a profile ~19 points
short per dimension trips 2 gaps at 35 easily) and stated as a partial fix
rather than reported as a success afterwards.

`displayBand` is unchanged because it never depended on the guardrail — the
user-visible picture was already fixed by the band work. This improved the
*internal* tier from a constant to something with signal; it did not transform
it.

### Not done — deliberately
Going further means raising the limit again (at some point the guardrail guards
nothing), or requiring 3+ gaps to cap (would uncap the 8 rows at 2 gaps → 14/32).
Both trade away the property the cap exists for, which is the point where it
needs an IO-psychologist rather than another config change.
**`BLUEPRINT_SME_SIGNOFF` stays false and the "decision support only — not a
validated selection instrument" banner stays up.** It is also possible the
guardrail is simply telling the truth: this profile genuinely is 25–40 points
short on several dimensions each role calls essential.

### Verified
- PR #808. Promote `release-stable-2026-08-04-critical-gap-limit`.
- Both Lambdas read `BLUEPRINT_CRITICAL_GAP_LIMIT=35`, `mean-gap`, `SME=false`.
- +5 tests; 140 scoring tests pass.
- **Pre-tag check earned its keep:** another terminal had promoted an honor
  import fix since the previous tag. All four prior promote tags
  (`honor-import-fk`, `fit-band`, `fit-tiers-and-prep`, `bio-sessions`) were
  verified as ancestors before tagging, so none of their work was reverted.

## [2026-08-04] — Seven interview/funnel fixes; two were silent failures

All seven live on dev and staging-b. Two had been failing invisibly — the code
ran, nothing errored, and the feature simply did not work.

### Fixed — the voice was mechanical because server TTS never ran
`useTTS` posted `/v1/audio/tts`, **a route that does not exist**. It 404s
(verified on dev), `fetchServerAudio` catches everything and returns null, and
every caller fell through to browser SpeechSynthesis. Nothing logged; the only
symptom was that it sounded synthetic.
- Repointed at `/v1/agents/voice/synthesize` — the endpoint MeridianChat already
  uses, via `agentApi` because `/v1/agents/*` does not route through the plain
  `api`. **Verified: 200, 85,248 bytes of audio/mpeg.**
- Voice default is now `MERIDIAN_VOICE` ("shimmer"), matching MeridianChat. It
  was "coral", which made the interview sound like a different assistant.
- **This affected every spoken surface** — Chronicle and Interview Practice were
  mechanical too, not just the goal interview.
- Files: `src/hooks/useTTS.ts`

### Fixed — the mic stopped listening mid-answer
`onend` set `listening=false` with nothing restarting it. The Web Speech API
ends a session after a second or two of silence, so the mic died the moment
someone paused to think and the few words captured became the whole answer.
- Recognition now restarts while the caller still wants to listen; stops only on
  an explicit stop or a fatal error (`not-allowed`, `audio-capture`).
- Auto-send moved from **2.5s after the last finalised phrase** to **6s after the
  last sign of speech of any kind**, interim included.
- `interimResults` on, so someone talking into a silent box can see it is
  hearing them. Also typed the Web Speech surface properly — 3 of those
  `no-explicit-any` lint errors pre-dated this change.
- Files: `src/hooks/interview/useSpeechDictation.ts`

### Added — the interview says how far through it is
Five areas stated up front with a progress bar; per-area question counts appear
once they are real. Promising "12 questions" then asking 17 would be worse than
saying nothing.

### Changed — "Draft my goals" reads as the primary action
Was a 7px ghost pill beside "Skip this area", indistinguishable from the
secondary controls despite being what the whole interview exists to reach.

### Fixed — "Job Matches all say Poor fit", in three layers
1. **Cut scores.** `licensed` does not discriminate: 480 of 480 (person, role)
   pairs classify as `misalignment` because the moderate-fit edge sits below the
   entire observed distribution. `BLUEPRINT_FIT_CALIBRATION='mean-gap'` on dev
   and staging-b.
2. **The display band never went through the calibration at all.** `_fit_band`
   banded raw total variation at the same 100/200/300 absolute cuts regardless
   of the flag — so it contradicted the number beside it: `fitScore: 81` next to
   `fitBand: "Poor"`, both from the same total variation, one normalised by
   dimension count and the other not. Band is now derived from the tier under
   the scheme in force.
3. **The guardrail caps every row and explained nothing.** `criticalGapCount` is
   now served so a surface can say "close, with 3 critical gaps" instead of an
   unexplained rejection.
- **Verified on dev:** `displayBand` went from **32 × Poor** to
  **3 Excellent · 7 Good · 7 Moderate · 15 Poor**; `criticalGapCount` populated
  (4 rows at 2, 14 at 3, 10 at 4, 4 at 5).
- **NOT changed, needs SME:** the guardrail thresholds themselves (benchmark ≥65
  missed by >25). Roles carry ~9 critical dimensions and essentially everyone
  trips 2, so `tier` still reads `misalignment` on all 32. Same defect as the cut
  scores one layer down; loosening a safety cap is not a change to make from a
  dashboard complaint. `BLUEPRINT_SME_SIGNOFF` stays false.

### Fixed — Interview Prep never worked, for one reason
`candidateId = user?.id`, and `AuthContext` seeds that to the literal string
`"me"`. The guide built against a candidate that cannot exist, **and** the
peek's `candidateId === candidateId` comparison could never match a real id — so
the page never rendered a sheet and the build button did nothing. Both reported
symptoms, one cause. The backend now resolves placeholder ids to the caller's
token subject via the existing `_sub(request)`; a recruiter passing a real id is
unaffected.

### Changed — My Plan builds on arrival
Someone who followed the link has already said what they want; an idle page with
a button asking "did you mean it?" read as broken. Fires once per mount, only
from idle, never auto-retrying a failure.

### Corrections — two things I got wrong
- **I called a failed dev CDK deploy "cosmetic".** It was not: `cdk deploy`
  matched no stack and deployed nothing. I mistook a coincidental
  `UPDATE_COMPLETE` — timestamped **seven seconds before my command started** —
  for confirmation. Reading a coincidence as evidence is the same error as
  trusting a green deploy.
- **The stack argument was wrong twice.** `BlueprintServiceStack` is the
  TypeScript class name; the CDK construct id is `ig-dev-blueprint`. Error:
  `No stacks match the name(s) BlueprintServiceStack`, only visible in the
  uploaded `cdk-deploy.log` artefact — GitHub's log API drops that output.
- Neither caused harm (the merge pipeline deployed dev; staging-b goes by
  promote), but both were green-ish signals read as proof.

### Verified
- +19 tests; 4 of 8 dictation tests confirmed failing on the old code.
- Frontend 4298 pass, build + ESLint clean. Backend compiles; CI green.
- PRs #806, #807 (backend), FE #361, #362. Promotes:
  `release-stable-2026-08-04-fit-tiers-and-prep`, `…-fit-band`.
- **Not observed:** the voice and mic in a real browser session. The endpoint
  returns real audio and the dictation logic is test-covered, but someone has to

### Fixed — the endpoint shipped on a prefix that never reaches it
**The bug worth remembering.** `POST /v1/documents/prism-report` answered **405**
while tests were green, CI green, deploy green, smoke probes green, and the code
was confirmed present *inside the running container*.
- API Gateway maps `/v1/documents/*` to the **document-service Lambda**, not the
  agent-engine. The route was live in a process nothing routes the request to.
- **Why the test missed it:** it asserted the path was in `router.routes`, which
  proves the mount *inside this app* and says nothing about which service the
  gateway targets. Its docstring even claimed the prefix was "verified live" —
  what was actually verified was that `GET /v1/documents/latest-prism` returns
  200, and agent-engine was **inferred** from that. Wrong: document-service
  implements that read too.
- Moved to `POST /v1/agents/documents/prism-report`
  (`POST /v1/agents/{proxy+}` → the agent-engine ALB). Test rewritten to assert
  the router is under `/v1/agents/*`, is **not** on the document-service prefix,
  and is actually `include_router`'d — mounting and forgetting to include is
  silent. Warning comment left on the module for the next person.
- **Nothing in the pipeline could have caught this.** Neither smoke suite covers
  `/v1/documents/*` or `/v1/agents/direction-setting/*`. Only calling the
  endpoint after the deploy found it.

Stage 5 was a door to `/summit/*`. Its own guard test said in a comment that

risk was two rival goal lists. The interview is no longer a surface —
`useSummitInterview` is a headless machine over `/ask`, `/why-ladder`,

store**. Still exactly one list, and the test now guards *that*.

- **A test caught a real defect:** the first version spoke only the newest turn,

## [2026-08-04] — Practitioner Workbench: design & functional specification

### Added
- **`IG_Practitioner_Workbench_Design_Spec.docx`** (11 pages) — design + functional spec for the Practitioner role page and sub-menus, covering Client Management, PRISM survey request/return, client-material ingestion, session prep, scheduling with Amazon Chime, and paid tool add-ons.
  - Generator: `scripts/build_practitioner_workbench_design.py` (python-docx, house palette, `Logo-Dark.png`, helpers reused verbatim from `build_video_meeting_decision_memo.py`). Render-verified via PDF → PNG.

### The finding that changes the estimate
"Ingest the client's material under the client's name with practitioner access enabled" is **not a UI change**. RAG retrieval scopes documents with a single-owner scalar equality — `services/agent-engine/app/rag/retriever.py:185`:
```sql
AND (d.user_id = :user_id OR d.user_id IS NULL OR d.user_id = '')
```
There is **no "shared with" relation anywhere in the schema**. That blunt filter was added 2026-05-13 (PR #103) to close a real leak where the `user_id` parameter was accepted and ignored. Three options assessed; recommendation is an explicit, revocable, consent-backed `document_access_grants` table plus an **optional** `accessible_user_ids` retriever parameter defaulting to today's behaviour — shipped behind a flag, because that function is on the path of every RAG call for every user in every vertical. Impersonation and duplication were both rejected, with reasons.

### Verified against code (not recalled)
- **Nine practitioner pages, eight nav items, zero client detail page.** `Clients.tsx` rows are not clickable; `practitioner.service.ts` exposes four GETs and no write path; "+ Add Client" has no `onClick`.
- **`Clients.tsx` renders `FALLBACK_CLIENTS`** — eight fabricated people with plausible names, employers and emails — on any API error, above four hard-coded summary tiles. Flagged as the first thing to delete: fabricated data is indistinguishable from working software in a demo.
- **The four practitioner endpoints are on the monolith** (`/api/practitioner/*`), which is being strangled — so this functionality needs a new home. Two options weighed; recommendation is to extend growth-service (#17) with a practitioner tenancy mode rather than stand up a nineteenth service, since a client roster is structurally the same object as a manager's direct reports.
- **Scheduling/Chime is already designed** — `docs/plans/IG_Live_Meetings_Build_Plan.md` specifies meeting-service #18 with `ChimeProvider` behind a `MeetingProvider` seam and names Practitioners as a mounting vertical. The spec mounts that rather than proposing a second meeting stack.
- **`prism_results` is the read store** — a practitioner-side import writing only the canonical tables is an invisible import (the #794 defect); the acceptance test must assert readability from the client page, not write success.

### Note
Written while the shared working directories sit on other terminals' feature branches, so the spec states that caveat on its own first page. **Not committed** — see the session entry.
  - Files: `IG_Practitioner_Workbench_Design_Spec.docx`, `scripts/build_practitioner_workbench_design.py`

## [2026-08-04] — cors-options was declared BELOW its measured load (25 → 250); staging-b now covered

Closes the top item of #798 — the only finding there with an active outage path.

### Fixed
- **`ig-*-cors-options` reserved concurrency 25 → 250, and `staging-b` added to the allowlist.**
  25 was **below** real preflight load, not above it. Measured `ConcurrentExecutions` Maximum at
  1-minute resolution: **dev peak 90** (95 invocations inside a single minute, 2026-07-20T15:40Z),
  **staging-b peak 124**. Both on near-idle environments.
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/api-gateway-stack.ts`

### Why 25 was there, and why it was wrong
The original comment read `// S7-A: floor reserved concurrency…`, and the CI gate enforcing that
convention is itself named "Reserved concurrency floor" (`pr-validation.yml:367`). The convention was
designed around a guaranteed **minimum**. AWS reserved concurrency is a floor **and** a ceiling at
once — there is no floor-only setting — so an intent to guarantee 25 silently capped at 25.

The judgement behind the number wasn't careless: per invocation the shim really is trivial (128 MB,
**3.7 ms average**, no I/O). What it misses is that preflight concurrency tracks **browser fan-out**,
not work per call. The 90-peak was 95 OPTIONS arriving in the same instant from one page's parallel
XHRs — each alive for milliseconds. Cheap and highly concurrent simultaneously.

### Why it never actually fired
Two accidents. `staging-b` was absent from the `['dev','staging','prod']` allowlist, and the
2026-07-06 concurrency wipe left dev's live function with no reservation at all. So the 25 existed
in the deployed template while the live function ran uncapped — **drifted into safety**. Any
CloudFormation update pulling that resource into a changeset would have re-asserted it.

### The ordering trap this removes
staging-b measured **higher than dev** (124 vs 90). Anyone tidying the 23 allowlists that omit
`staging-b` — the same omission fixed in #764 and #793 — would have propagated a 25-cap to the
busiest environment. That is now safe by construction: the value was fixed **and** `staging-b` added
in one atomic change, with 250 ≈ 2× staging-b's observed peak.

### Sizing rationale
250 is ~2× the highest observed anywhere. On dev it is not even reachable: the API Gateway stage
burst limit is **100** (`config.ts` `apiThrottle`, set in #764), which is why dev tops out near 90 —
the Gateway is the real bound there, and the reservation now sits above it by design rather than
below it by accident. Account cost: 250 of ~750 unreserved per env.

Undersizing here does not degrade gracefully. It throttles CORS preflight, which surfaces as the
browser being unable to reach the API at all — and reads like an auth or networking fault rather
than a Lambda concurrency cap.

### Added
- `infrastructure/cdk/test/cors-options-concurrency.test.ts` — 9 assertions pinning the value against
  the **measured peaks** rather than a magic number, so an undersizing edit fails with a message
  explaining why the number matters. Includes an explicit guard that 25 cannot return.
  **Verified non-vacuous**: reverting to the original declaration fails 8 of 9.

### Known — still open in #798
- The CI "Reserved concurrency floor" gate counts **occurrences** of `reservedConcurrentExecutions:`
  (`>= 20`), not values. It can never catch a wrong number — which is exactly how a value 3.6× under
  real load passed review. Unchanged here.
- 18 declared-but-unset functions, `audit-service` throttling, and the shared-account topology
  question all remain.

## [2026-08-04] — Fix: magic-link sessions couldn't refresh → ~30-min forced logout (staging-b)

Diagnosed and fixed the "staging-b logs me out after ~30 min whether active or not" report.

### Root cause (confirmed against live staging-b auth-service logs)
Users sign into staging-b via **magic-link** (`POST /v1/magic-link/verify 200`), which issues an
**HS256 refresh token the auth-service signed itself**. But `/v1/refresh-token` only ever exchanged
tokens with **Cognito** — so it sent the HS256 token to Cognito, got `invalid_grant` (400), and the
frontend interceptor treated the failed refresh as "session over" (`clearAuth()` → `/login`). Magic-link
sessions therefore could never be renewed and died at the access token's lifetime (~30 min on the
deployed staging-b) — idle or active, since any background request 401s at expiry and triggers the
doomed refresh. Log evidence: a stream of `POST /v1/refresh-token 400` + `Cognito token refresh failed:
{"error":"invalid_grant"}`; a magic-link login at 20:25:06 → first refresh-fail at 20:55:19 (~30 min).

### Fixed
- `services/auth-service/app/routes/refresh_token.py` — `/v1/refresh-token` now recognises our own HS256
  refresh tokens (`token_use == "refresh"`, signed with `settings.secret_key`) and **mints a fresh HS256
  access token locally**, so a magic-link session lasts for the life of its 30-day refresh token. Opaque
  Cognito refresh tokens fail that decode and fall through to the **unchanged** Cognito path.
- Mono **PR #810** (`5fe902f4`). 3 new tests (`tests/test_token.py`); existing refresh/magic/login/jwt
  suites (51 tests) green.

### Deploy
- **dev**: merge #810 → Staged-Deploy-on-merge (auth-service Lambda). **staging-b**: pending a
  `release-stable-*` tag promote (backend reaches staging-b only by tag) — awaiting go.

### Latent follow-up (not this bug)
The `ig-staging-b-auth-service` Lambda role lacks `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue` on the magic-auth JWT
secret and falls back to the `SECRET_KEY` env var (works today because they match). Worth granting the
role read on the secret in CDK.

## [2026-08-04] — Fix: Honor coach assessment import 500/503 (assessments FK vs self-subject fellow)

Diagnosed and fixed a coach ([user P.G.]) getting a **503** importing a fellow's
PRISM / DISC / CliftonStrengths on the Honor Coach Workbench. Backend PR #809,
merge `74d0bebd`; shipped + ECS-exec-verified on **dev** (task def :54) AND
**staging-b** (tag `release-stable-2026-08-04-honor-import-fk` → staging-b-promote,
all jobs green incl. authenticated smoke, task def :22, `desiredCount=1`). No
migration in the delta.

### Fixed
- **Coach assessment import 500 → 503 for any coach-managed/invited fellow.**
  `honor.py:post_coach_assessment_import_route` → `profile.py:_write_assessment_rows`
  wrote `assessments.user_id = <fellow_id>`, but an Honor fellow is a *self-subject*
  (`linked_user_sub == fellow_id`) with **no `public.users` row**, and
  `assessments.user_id` has a hard FK → `users(user_id)`. So every import hit
  `assessments_user_id_fkey` → 500 (surfaced as 503); retries spawned duplicate
  fellow rows. It only ever "worked" for `fellow_kind='linked'` fellows (id == a

  row (`is_active=false`, synthetic unique `honor-fellow+{id}@fellows.honor.invalid`
  email, default `auth_provider`, `ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO NOTHING`) keyed to the
  fellow's own id. Satisfies the FK; can never authenticate.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/tools/honor/coach.py`
- `_ensure_import_subject_user()` on the coach import **write path only** (never on
  `/preview`, so preview stays side-effect-free), with a defensive re-check that
  degrades an unprovisionable subject to a clean **409** instead of an FK 500.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/routes/honor.py`

### Changed
- `convert_fellow` (managed→invited) now also provisions the non-login shadow user
  when it sets the self-subject link — so future invited fellows are import-safe at

  (profile + coach link; 0 assessments existed). [user P.G.] must **re-run** the three
  imports (earlier attempts rolled back — 0 rows persisted); his résumé/CareerLeader
  documents did persist.

### Tests

  `ensure_subject_user` unit incl. bad-uuid) + updated invite-flow test for the new
  shadow-user INSERT. **378 passed / 3 skipped** across the honor + profile suites.

## [2026-08-03] — W1 + W7 shipped to dev and staging-b; a near-miss rollback caught in the queue

Deployment half of the W1/W7 work logged in the entry below. Both PRs merged,
both environments carrying it, and one incident worth reading before the next
multi-terminal promote.

### Changed — merged and deployed
- **`inspire-genius#800`** (backend) and **`inspire-genius-frontend#354`** (frontend)
  merged to `development` after waiting for green — backend went `UNSTABLE` →
  `CLEAN` before merging rather than merging over an in-progress gate.
- Dev: agent-engine rolled, W1 + W7 confirmed in the running container.
- staging-b: **`release-stable-2026-08-03-goal-store-bridge`** promoted #796
  (stage-6 goal store bridge), pinned to `a184ef93` so it carried only what was
  authorised. 6/6 jobs green.
- staging-b: #800 reached staging-b via another terminal's
  **`release-stable-2026-08-03-assessment-import`** tag, which already contained
  it. FE/BE mismatch closed.

### Fixed — a queued promote would have reverted another terminal's work
Tagged `21f7aa12` (#800) for staging-b **while another terminal's promote of
`ea8e1511` (#801) was already 12 minutes into the queue**. Their tag contained
#800; **my tag did not contain #801**. The workflow serialises promotes
(`concurrency: staging-b-promote`, `cancel-in-progress: false`), so mine was
queued to run *after* theirs and would have deployed an image built before #801
existed — silently undoing their profile-import fix minutes after it landed.
- **Caught by asking why my run said `pending` rather than `in_progress`**,
  instead of treating "triggered" as "done".
- Run cancelled before it began deploying; stale tag deleted from remote and
  local and the deletion verified.
- **The lesson is not "pin tags" or "don't pin".** Pinning was right for #796
  (it kept unverified work off staging-b) and wrong here (`development` had
  moved underneath me, so pinning became a rollback). The rule is: **check what
  is already in flight before tagging**, and coordinate with the terminal that
  owns the intervening commits.

### Verified — and the false pass that was nearly reported
- **Nearly reported a green result from the wrong code.** At 18:59 the staging-b
  edge returned 200/204 — from the task that started **08:05 that morning**, on
  the old digest; the new image was still `PENDING`. Those same codes appear with
  the bug fully present. Every verification below therefore checks *which task is
  serving* before trusting anything it says.
- staging-b final state: ECR `:latest` `48995d9c…`, single RUNNING/HEALTHY task on
  that digest, old task drained. In-container: **13** `"optional":` flags (exactly
  one per stage), `PRODUCED_BY` ×3, `unmet_needs` ×5 in the serialiser,
  `why_roots` ×4 in `routes/goals.py`, `summit_store` ×2 in `alignment.py`
  (#796 survived, not clobbered). Edge 200 / 204 preflight / 401 on both
  `/journey` and `/goals/session`.
- Dev, W1 **live end to end**: `GET /journey` serves `optional`, `unmetNeeds` and
  `reachable` per stage; `nextAction` resolves to a required, reachable stage.
- **The smoke matrix does not cover stage 6.** Read the workflow rather than
  assuming: its route list has no `/v1/agents/direction-setting/*` probe at all.
  A green smoke gate means staging-b is broadly healthy — it is **not** evidence
  for #796 or #800.

### Open — stated rather than rounded up
- **W7 at runtime is unverified in both environments.** Code presence is confirmed
  on dev and staging-b; a live root-write has been observed nowhere. The 5 unit
  tests were confirmed failing on the prior code — that is test evidence, not an
  observed result.
- **W1's skip behaviour is unit-test-proven only.** The dev account already has
  every optional stage complete, so live data cannot exercise the skip.
- Two verification steps were declined mid-session (an unscoped multi-user goal
  query — correctly refused, it read ten users' rows to answer a question about
  one account — and a later scoped read). The scoped read stalled on schema I

## [2026-08-03] — User roster generators (dev + staging-b), .docx and .xlsx

### Added
- `scripts/build_ig_user_roster.py` — Word roster (landscape, repeating header
  row, brand palette, logo).
- `scripts/build_ig_user_roster_xlsx.py` — Excel roster: frozen header,
  autofilter across all columns, plus a Summary sheet.
- Columns: First name · Last name · Email · Environment · Primary profile ·
  Status · Added (EDT). **289 accounts** (stable 105, dev 184).

### Guarded — the migration-runner row cap
The runner caps returned **rows at 10**, so a naive roster query would have
returned 10 users and looked entirely healthy. Both environments are
aggregated **server-side into a single `jsonb` value**, and the fetch step
**asserts the returned length equals `COUNT(*)`** per environment, refusing to
build a partial roster. Both matched (105 / 184).

### Decisions worth keeping
- **Soft-deleted accounts are included and marked, not dropped.** Dev holds 70
  of them; filtering to active would have quietly turned "all users" into 217
  instead of 289.
- **Unnamed accounts sort last.** The first build sorted purely by surname,
  which pushed every blank-name account to the front and made page 1 a wall of
  dashes — caught by rendering the PDF, not by reading the source.
- Blank names are shown as-is rather than derived from the email address;
  inventing names in a roster is worse than an honest blank.
- One dev account has a genuinely NULL `created_at`; it reads **"unknown"**
  rather than blank so it does not look like a formatting glitch.
- `Added (EDT)` is written as a **real datetime** in the workbook (not text) so
  Excel's date filters and chronological sort work; the UTC→`America/New_York`
  conversion happens once in SQL.

### Not committed — deliberately
The generated `.docx` / `.xlsx` hold **289 real users' names and emails**. Both
are gitignored; only the generators are in the tree. Intermediate JSON and
render artefacts were deleted after use.

### Verified
Workbook **read back after writing**: 289 rows, 0 blank emails, 288 real
datetimes + 1 "unknown", autofilter `A1:G290`, per-environment totals matching
the live DB exactly. Word version rendered to PDF→PNG and inspected.

## [2026-08-03] — CORRECTION: the "delay is inside HostMonster" conclusion was overstated

Supersedes the causal claim in *"Live A/B delivery test settles it: the delay is inside
HostMonster, after acceptance"* earlier today. **The mechanism is not established. The ticket is
on hold.**

### What prompted the correction
Bill supplied full headers from a delivered magic-link message. Decoded:

```
DKIM t=1785805438  → SES signed/sent      2026-08-04 01:03:58 UTC
Received (esmtps)  → shared107 accepted   2026-08-04 01:04:40 UTC   (+42s in transit)
Received (LMTP)    → shared107 → mailbox  2026-08-04 01:04:40 UTC   (same second)
Delivery-Date                              2026-08-04 01:04:40 UTC   (same second)
```

One external hop, no intermediate relay, and **HostMonster's internal queue time was zero** —
SMTP-in, LMTP hand-off and Delivery-Date all stamped the same second. Spam scoring was not
marginal either: `X-Spam-Flag: NO`, `X-Spam-Status: score=-0.7`, `X-Spam-Score: -6`,
`Delivered-To: [email redacted]` — negative scores, straight to the inbox.

### ⚠️ But the sample is a FAST message — confirmed by Bill
**This header is from a message that was NOT slow.** It therefore shows the path *can* be clean;
it does **not** describe what happens on a slow delivery. Reading it as a refutation would be the
same error in the opposite direction.

### What is actually established vs. not
| claim | status |
|---|---|
| SES is not the bottleneck | **Established** — Send == Delivery, 0 bounces, 0 rejects, **0 DeliveryDelay** over 7 days and across the A/B test |
| HostMonster accepts first-attempt, never defers | **Established** — 0 DeliveryDelay means no `4xx`; greylisting ruled out |
| Gmail instant, @3pp.com slow, same sender/instant | **Established** — the A/B test |
| Custom MAIL FROM + new sender live in production | **Established** — `Return-Path: …@noreply.inspiresgenius.com`, DKIM `d=inspiresgenius.com` selector `hxpms2x5…` (staging-b token) |
| Messages are not being spam-quarantined | **Established** (for this sample) |
| **The delay happens inside shared107 after acceptance** | **NOT established** — asserted earlier on inference, never measured on a slow message |
| Mail-client fetch interval as the cause | **Plausible, untested** — a 15-min IMAP poll would produce exactly this symptom |

### Why the original entry was wrong to state it as settled
The A/B test proved *where the delay is not* (not SES, not transit, not greylisting) and left one
region unmeasured: everything past SMTP acceptance. That region contains **both** HostMonster's
queue **and** the recipient's mail client. The entry named the first as the cause when the
evidence could not distinguish them. Classic narrowing-to-a-favoured-hypothesis; the honest
statement was always "the delay is downstream of AWS acceptance, mechanism unknown."

### Consequence — ticket held, not sent
`docs/support/HostMonster_Inbound_Delay_Ticket.md` argued the post-acceptance claim as its central
point. **Had it been sent, HostMonster would have produced this exact header and closed the
case.** Marked HOLD at the top and its claims restated to match the evidence. It becomes sendable
the moment we have headers from a message observed to be slow.

### What settles it
Headers from a **slow** delivery, plus the wall-clock minute it became visible. Compare
`Delivery-Date` against that:
- gap on the server (Delivery-Date late) → HostMonster queue; the ticket is right after all.
- gap after the server (Delivery-Date early, seen late) → the message sat in the mailbox and the
  **mail client** was not fetching. Device setting, no ticket warranted.

### Resolved and dropped
**Inbox vs Junk** — answered by these headers: `Delivered-To` plus `X-Spam-Flag: NO`. Inbox. No
longer an open question.

## [2026-08-03] — W1 + W7: the funnel stops stalling, and the interview finally runs

Built the two workstreams the Summit wiring plan named as "the product". Both
were cases of working machinery with nothing driving it.

### Fixed — W1: an optional stage read as mandatory and stalled the funnel
`next_action` returned the first incomplete stage in order, full stop. Stage 2
(Self-Portrait) is an insight page nothing depends on, so it sat in front of
anyone who had not read it — and **goals, job matches, plan and interview prep
behind it were never offered.** That is the reported "My Goals blocks all that
follows", from the server side.
- Stages now declare `optional`. The required spine is the product's stated
  funnel: `0 → 1 → 3 → 5 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 11 → 12`.
- `PRODUCED_BY` maps each `needs` entry to the stage that satisfies it, so a
  stage's outstanding requirements are **computed rather than restated**.
- `next_action` prefers a required stage that can run now, falls back to a
  runnable optional one, and names a blocked stage rather than claiming
  completion. `to_dict` serves `optional` / `unmetNeeds` / `reachable`.
- `blueprints` maps to **no** producer deliberately — role benchmarks are
  supplied by the org, not earned. Treating them as earnable would mark Target
  and Gap unreachable for every user forever.
- **Nothing locks.** Every stage stays enterable; this changes what is
  *offered*, not what is permitted.
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/tools/direction_setting/{stages,journey}.py`

### Fixed — W7: the WHY-ladder root was computed and thrown away
`synthesize_goals` reads `session["why_roots"]` to give each goal its
motivation. **Nothing ever appended to that list.** Every ladder run was
discarded the moment it was rendered, and synthesis fell back to inferring
motivation from the transcript. The live dev session with **7 goals and 0
why_roots** is exactly what that looks like from outside.
- `POST /why-ladder` now persists the root against its stated goal, replacing
  rather than duplicating on a re-run. Best-effort — a failed save is logged and
  never fails the turn.
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/routes/goals.py`

### Added — W7: a driver for the interview that was already built
The three structured routes (`/ask`, `/why-ladder`, `/synthesize`) were built,
deployed and working, and **nothing in the product called them**.
`goals.service.ts` exposed only view-and-edit. Summit offered generic Meridian
chat and hoped intent classification landed on the right specialist.
- `useSummitInterview` walks the five categories a question at a time, banks
  each, asks for a stated goal in one sentence, ladders it to a root, then
  synthesises. **Deterministic** — it always knows the category, the question
  and the rung, which is the whole argument for driving the routes directly
  instead of posting free text at a classifier.
- We ask for the stated goal **ourselves**. Picking one out of the model's own
  questions would mean guessing which generated question was the goal one —
  the exact ambiguity the structured routes exist to remove.
- The rung cap is enforced client-side **as well as** server-side. Trusting a
  remote loop bound to be enforced remotely is how an interview becomes an
  interrogation.
- Files: `src/hooks/summit/useSummitInterview.ts`,
  `src/components/summit/SummitInterviewPanel.tsx`,
  `src/services/summit/goals.service.ts`, `src/types/summit.ts`

### Changed — the interview is on IG's chrome, not Summit's fork
Built on the shared shadcn tokens the rest of IG uses (the set
`ChronicleChatPanel` already sits on), not Summit's parallel
`components/ui.tsx` and hard-coded teal. Growing that fork to fit the interview
would have doubled the surface anyone maintaining IG chat has to keep in step.
- The panel also stops being **desktop-only**. It was `hidden lg:flex` —
  defensible for an optional chat companion, not once it is how goals get made.
- Journey map: renders `unmetNeeds` rather than `needs`, so a stage stops saying
  *"thin without your PRISM results"* to someone whose PRISM has been on file
  for weeks. Optional stages are labelled. Falls back to `needs` on an older
  backend.
- Discovery shows the person's **own** WHY roots once the ladder has run, and
  keeps the worked example only while there are none.
- Files: `src/pages/summit/{SummitLayout,SummitDiscovery}.tsx`,
  `src/pages/direction-setting/JourneyPage.tsx`, `src/types/direction-setting.ts`

### Verified
- **+43 tests, each checked to fail on the prior code** — not assumed. The old
  `next_action` was run directly against the symptom: it returned stage 2 after
  Establish, and its walk interleaved the optional stages.
- Agent-engine: **4452 passed** vs **4430** on an untouched baseline (+22). The
  171 pre-existing websocket/auth failures were measured on *both* sides rather
  than waved at.
- Frontend: **4265 passed** / 541 suites, `npm run build` and ESLint clean.
- A test caught a real bug: a failed `/ask` pushed an error turn, which retired
  the empty state and the Start button with it — stranding the person behind the
  very message saying nothing was lost. Fixed with a retry.
- Two existing backend tests encoded the old rule. One, docstring *"should be
  sent back to 5"*, asserted `"4"`: **the docstring had described the intended
  behaviour all along and only the assertion disagreed.**

### Open / not done
- **Not merged, not deployed.** PRs `inspire-genius#800` (backend) and
  `inspire-genius-frontend#354` (frontend). A frontend merge deploys to dev
  **and staging-b**, which wants a deliberate decision given tonight's promote.

  class of bug, flagged not fixed.
- W2–W6 of the plan untouched.

## [2026-08-03] — CORRECTION: the outstanding PRISM user cannot be fixed by re-import

The 2026-08-03 dual-store entry said the one un-backfillable user needed her

- the other two variant rows are entirely blank
- a well-formed export has **three labelled rows** (verified against 13 others)

### Ruled out — position cannot identify the variant
The tempting inference is "it is row 0, so it is Underlying". Surveyed all 13
well-formed exports: **10 lead with `Adapted`, 3 with `Underlying`**. Row
position carries no information here.

### Not done, deliberately
Her 8 quadrant behaviours ARE present and numeric, so `derive_colours` would
run and her profile would load immediately. The sole blocker is not knowing
which variant the numbers are — and `prism_results` is read as the
**authoritative profile platform-wide** (chat injection, dashboard, Job Fit),
so loading an unknown variant would quietly misrepresent a real person's
natural style as adapted behaviour, or vice versa.

**Decision (Bill): obtain a fresh complete export from the PRISM portal**
rather than infer. Loading the existing row as Underlying was explicitly
rejected. Once the export exists it goes through `admin_csv_upload`, which now
writes both stores, and takes about two minutes.

Nothing else is wrong with her account or the pipeline — she is the only
remaining case on either environment.

## [2026-08-03] — Summit's directed interview is built but nothing drives it (W7 added to the plan)

Asked how the goal-setting process is meant to work — *"a directed interview session that drives to the why of the goal."* It is exactly that, it is built, and the frontend does not call it.

### Findings
- **The interview engine exists and works.** Five discovery categories (Career History → Current Job → Workplace → Ambitions → Personal) behind three live routes:
  - `POST /ask/{category}` — warm intro + contextual questions, PRISM-anchored. Stance is explicit: *"exploration, not interrogation… warm, concise, one-thread-at-a-time."*
  - `POST /why-ladder` — the directed part. Asks *why* for **3–5 rungs**, stopping at "a value, identity, or emotional root", hard-capped at 5 so it cannot badger. Returns `{is_root, question, root}`.
  - `POST /synthesize` — captured answers + PRISM → structured goals, each carrying `motivation` (defined in schema as *"the WHY-ladder root / why it truly matters"*), `prism_alignment` (leverages_strength / requires_stretch / counterbalance), an `execution_style` keyed to quadrant, a `success_metric`, and a `first_step` framed "non-threatening, reward-framed".
  - Verified live: `/why-ladder` returned *"What draws you toward operations — what do you picture yourself doing once you're in that role?"*
- **Nothing in the product drives it.** `goals.service.ts` exposes only `getGoalSession`, `patchGoal`, `deleteGoal` — view and edit. The frontend calls **none** of `/ask`, `/why-ladder`, `/synthesize`. `SummitDiscovery` displays category status; it does not run the interview. The only conversational path is generic Meridian chat, not the structured Summit loop.
- **The evidence is in the live session:** **7 goals, 0 `why_roots`.** The ladder has never run for this user. Those goals were written, not excavated — titles with no root motivation underneath, which is precisely what the stage exists to produce.

### Changed
- **Corrected the plan issued earlier today.** `Summit_My_Goals_Wiring_Plan.docx` assessed which pages were on mock data but did **not** check whether the interview loop was *driven*, so "wire the interview" was missing from W1–W6. That is a real omission in a costed plan, recorded rather than quietly patched.
  - **W7 — wire the Summit interview loop: 3 man-days / 3 CC sessions.** Service methods for the three routes, a discovery runner walking the five categories, the WHY-ladder as a turn-taking component, and synthesize-on-completion writing back to the store.
  - Revised total: **12.5 man-days / 13 CC sessions** (was 9.5 / 10).
  - **Resequenced:** W1 first still holds (half a day, unblocks the reported symptom), but W7 now comes **before** W2/W3 — W7 is what makes My Goals real; the Prism and Documents pages are presentation next to it.
  - Document not regenerated, deliberately: it may already be under review, and silently overwriting a document someone is marking up is worse than an entry saying what changed.
  - **Reissued** `Summit_My_Goals_Wiring_Plan.docx` with W7 folded in (generator `dab4db06`, render-verified, 5 pages). W7 carries two specifics: replace the **generic Meridian chat** path with the **structured Summit loop** (the loop is deterministic — known category, known rung, known next call — so it drives the three routes directly rather than inferring intent from free text), and build the UI on **IG stable chrome** rather than Summit's bespoke `MeridianPanel.tsx` / `ui.tsx`, retiring that parallel chat surface instead of growing it. Headline pairing in the reissue: **W1 + W7 = 3.5 days** is what makes My Goals real; everything else is presentation next to it.

## [2026-08-03] — Summit / My Goals wiring plan: two premises in the brief were wrong

Asked for a costed plan to make My Goals real, on the stated basis that it is unwired and **blocks Job Matches, My Plan, Interview Prep and Practise Answers**. Verified both claims against dev before planning, because a plan built on either would have bought the wrong thing.

### Findings
- **My Goals does not block the stages after it.** `goals` appears in exactly **one** stage's `needs` in `stages.py` — stage 6, Align. Stages 7–12 depend on prism, blueprints, gaps, plan, salary and guide. Demonstrated, not merely read: stages **7, 8, 9 and 10 all completed** on dev today on a journey where stage 5 was `not_started` and stage 6 `in_progress`.
  - What *is* true: `next_action` returns the first incomplete stage, so everyone is funnelled to My Goals regardless of what else is reachable. That is a **navigation defect (~0.5 d)**, not a reason to rebuild Summit.
- **The Summit backend is not unwired.** All eight `/v1/agents/goals/*` routes are live on dev, including the three LLM-backed ones — `POST /ask` and `POST /why-ladder` were called during the review and returned real, contextual content, not stubs.
- **The real gap is narrower than reported:** 3 of 8 Summit pages still read `summitData.ts` (SummitPrism, SummitProgress, SummitDocuments) — and **all three already carry a `SampleNotice`**, so they declare themselves rather than pretending. The other five consume live hooks.
- **One genuinely absent capability:** nothing tracks goal progress over time, which is what SummitProgress' `MILESTONES` / `DELTAS` mock stands in for.

### Added
- `docs/plans/Summit_My_Goals_Wiring_Plan.docx` — 6 workstreams, **9.5 man-days / 10 CC sessions** total, with the recommendation to ship **W1 alone (0.5 d)** and re-look, since W4 (goal progress) is 40% of the cost and may not survive the re-rank once the funnel stops pointing at an optional stage.
  - Generator: `scripts/build_summit_wiring_plan.py`. Render-verified to PDF/PNG — 4 pages, no overflow.
  - `*.docx` is gitignored repo-wide, so the generator is committed and the binary is not; it is reproducible in one command.

### Fixed (doc tooling)
- The shared `table()` helper now emits `w:tblLayout` **fixed**. Without it the renderer redistributes columns evenly and per-cell widths are silently ignored — which is what mangled the workstream table on the first two renders. Caught only because the document was rendered and read rather than trusted to a clean script exit.

## [2026-08-03] — Live A/B delivery test: SES ruled out (⚠️ SUPERSEDED IN PART — see the CORRECTION entry above; the "delay is inside HostMonster" causal claim is NOT established)

Bill: *"send me a test magic link and time it."* Ran a controlled experiment on both tiers, then
wrote the support ticket the result calls for. **This closes the diagnosis.**

### The experiment
Four magic-link requests fired **in parallel, within 13 ms of each other** — dev and staging-b ×
{`[email redacted]`, a personal Gmail address}. Same sending system, same SES account, same
instant; the **only** variable was the receiving mail infrastructure. Harness:
`scratchpad/maillink_timing.sh`.

| tier | recipient | SES accepted (UTC) | `accepted=True` |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev | Gmail | 04:39:58.350 | ✅ |
| dev | [email redacted] | 04:39:58.963 | ✅ |
| staging-b | Gmail | 04:40:03.413 | ✅ |
| staging-b | [email redacted] | 04:40:03.490 | ✅ |

Zero `unknown/inactive` warnings — all four accounts live in both databases, nothing silently
no-opped. **That confirmation line had never once been written before this week's log fix**; it
is the instrument that made this test readable at all.

### SES side: clean, on both tiers
| | dev | staging-b |
|---|---|---|
| Send / Delivery | 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 (both in the send minute) |
| **DeliveryDelay** | **0** | **0** |
| Bounce / Reject | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

SES records `Delivery` only on a `250 OK` from the receiving MTA, and `DeliveryDelay` whenever it
must retry after a deferral. **Zero DeliveryDelay ⇒ HostMonster accepted every message on the
first attempt, within a minute, and never deferred.** Greylisting is definitively ruled out.

### Result — and the conclusion
**Gmail arrived instantly. `@3pp.com` took minutes.** Since HostMonster *accepted* the messages
in the same minute, the entire delay sits **after SMTP acceptance** — inbound scanning or mailbox
queueing on `shared107`. **No AWS-side change can reach it.**

### ⚠️ Honest accounting on this week's work
- **The TTL 300 → 900s change was the fix that mattered.** A multi-minute mailbox queue against a
  5-minute expiry is exactly why links were dead on arrival. Resolved.
- **The sender move to `noreply@inspiresgenius.com` did NOT improve arrival time.** Cross-domain
  was a sound hypothesis, correctly executed, and the evidence says same-domain was not the
  cause. It remains a net improvement — SPF now aligns for DMARC instead of passing on DKIM
  alone, removing a real spam-scoring input — but it bought no speed and is not claimed to.
- **The log fix is what made the diagnosis possible**, twice over.

### Deliverables
`docs/support/HostMonster_Inbound_Delay_Ticket.md` + branded `.docx` (3 pp., logo, NAVY/TEAL/GOLD,
generated by the existing `scripts/build_candidate_interview_coach_docx.py` — it already accepts
SRC/OUT args, so no new generator). Structured to pre-empt "it's your sender": the A/B isolates
the receiving side, DeliveryDelay=0 kills greylisting, and it **volunteers the apex-MX error up
front** rather than letting support find it and deflect — while stating why it isn't the cause.

**Render-verified** (LibreOffice → PDF → PNG → read), which caught **two layout bugs invisible in
the source**: the metadata header had collapsed into a run-on paragraph, and the page-3 list was
numbered **4–7** because Word continued numbering from an earlier list. Both fixed and re-verified.

### Gap found, not fixed
`send_magic_link_email` **discards the SES response**, so no `MessageId` is logged. If HostMonster
asks for message IDs to trace, we cannot supply them retroactively — the test would have to be
re-run. Logging the MessageId is small and clearly worth doing before the next round.

### Privacy note (pre-existing, NOT introduced here)
A personal Gmail address appears **4× in `inspire-genius-frontend/change_log.md` and 1× in the
public `IG_project_log.html`** — and that frontend repo is **PUBLIC** (`willb77/inspire-genius-frontend`;
the monorepo is private). It dates from PRs #113/#114 where it was set as `alarmEmail`. Low
severity — it is Bill's own address, used for alarm notifications — but it is PII in a public
repo. **This entry deliberately does not add another occurrence.** Scrubbing published history is
Bill's call, not a unilateral fix.

### Still open
- **`3pp.com` apex MX** — delete `10 feedback-smtp.us-east-1.amazonses.com` from the apex only.
  HostMonster DNS; no AWS API reaches it.
- **File the ticket.** This is now the only lever left on real-world arrival time.
- **Unknown: Inbox vs Junk** for the delayed messages. Junk ⇒ scoring; Inbox-but-late ⇒ queue
  latency. Different conversations with support.
- **`Received:` headers** from a delayed message would be the most persuasive artifact — they are
  HostMonster's own hop timestamps.
- Shared hosting may simply be the ceiling. If support won't tune it, the durable fix is moving
  `@3pp.com` mailboxes to Google Workspace — the Gmail arm demonstrated exactly what that feels
  like on the same sending path.

## [2026-08-03] — PRISM admin writes now land in prism_results (the store the app reads)

Monorepo PR **#794**, merged as **`dd43b142`**; Staged Deploy run
`30786467340` green to **dev** (staging behind its manual gate).

### Fixed — imports were invisible to the entire application
`assessments` / `assessment_scores` is the canonical assessment store, but a
repo-wide grep found **no runtime code reads it** — `routes/prism.py`,
`memory/long_term.py`, `rag/prism_vectorizer.py` and dashboard-service all
read `prism_results`. Admin imports wrote only the canonical tables, so a
complete, authoritative 107-row PRISM import produced **nothing the user could
see**: no scores in chat, on the dashboard or in RAG, and
`GET /v1/documents/latest-prism` returning 404 — while the data looked
perfectly healthy in SQL. Two staging-b users were in exactly that state.
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/routes/profile_admin.py`

### Added — `_project_to_prism_results()`
- Colours derived via `prism_canon.derive_colours` — **the same function the
  app reads through**, not a second SQL copy of the quadrant pairing. That
  pairing has been rotated once already; a divergent reimplementation is how
  such a bug becomes permanent.
- Wired into **all three** admin write paths (create, import-csv, reprocess),
  not just the CSV import. `reprocess` regenerates scores, so without it
  `prism_results` would be left holding **stale** colours.
- Idempotent: `uuid5(ns, "user_id:assessment_id")` + `ON CONFLICT`.
  `prism_results` has no unique key on `user_id` and readers take
  `ORDER BY assessed_at DESC`, so a duplicate would be silently ambiguous.
- **Incomplete dimension sets write nothing** — a partial profile renders a
  misleading radar chart, worse than an obviously-absent one.
- `raw_data.dimensions` populated so the `long_term.py` read-path self-heal
  can recompute colours if the pairing ever changes again.

### Fixed — ORM/schema drift on `prism_results`
`created_at` + `updated_at` were added to the live tables by
`r29_prism_results_audit_columns.sql` but never mirrored into the ORM model,
so SQLite test tables lacked both while Postgres had them — the same class of
drift that previously shipped a 500. Deliberately no `onupdate=` (ORM
`onupdate` on an async session raises `MissingGreenlet`).
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/memory/models.py`

### Added — backfill for rows written before the fix
`scripts/backfill_prism_results_from_assessments.py`: dry-run by default,
idempotent, and it **reports users it cannot fix rather than silently
omitting them**.

## [2026-08-03] — ws-proxy ran uncapped on staging-b (Lambda blast-radius cap)

### Fixed
- **`ws-proxy` had no reserved concurrency on staging-b**, so nothing bounded how much of the
  account's Lambda pool the WebSocket path could consume. Every inbound WS message becomes one
  ws-proxy invocation held open for the whole agent turn (~20s typical, 120s timeout) — it calls
  agent-engine synchronously over the ALB. The only other bound was the API Gateway stage throttle
  of 25 msg/s, and **25/s × ~20s ≈ 500 concurrent — most of the ~800 unreserved pool.** A WS flood
  would have starved every other Lambda in the account (auth, documents, invitations): a chat
  problem presenting as a platform outage, in services unrelated to chat.
  - Cause: the allowlist read `['dev', 'staging', 'prod'].includes(envName)`. staging-b's `envName`
    is `'staging-b'`, so it fell to `undefined` — **the same omission shape as #764's throttle tier**,
    where `envName === 'staging'` never matched `'staging-b'`.
  - Headroom checked before changing it: staging-b had 793 of 1000 unreserved, so +25 leaves 768,
    far above the 100 floor AWS enforces. That floor is not theoretical here — the 2026-05-24
    staging-b bootstrap failed with `ig-staging-b-services` unable to deploy because reservations
    pushed the account under it.
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts`

### Added
- `infrastructure/cdk/test/ws-proxy-concurrency.test.ts` — 9 assertions across all four envs, plus
  a check that the cap stays below what the WS throttle could actually drive, and that ws-proxy's
  120s timeout (the thing that makes the cap necessary) is still there. **Verified the test fails
  against the old code**: reverting the allowlist fails exactly the four staging-b assertions and
  leaves dev/staging/prod green — which is also the evidence the change didn't move those three.

### Known — NOT fixed, needs a decision
- **dev's ws-proxy has live drift and the removal looks deliberate.** CloudFormation drift detection
  on `WsProxyFunction8B8A7A15` reports `/ReservedConcurrentExecutions` **expected 25, actual null,
  REMOVE** — the deployed template sets 25 but the live function has none. Alongside it, an
  out-of-band tag: `Audit: dormant-review-20260704`. Something classified ws-proxy as dormant on
  2026-07-04 and stripped its reservation, presumably to reclaim pool. ws-proxy is **not** dormant —
  it measured 16 messages/hour on dev the day before this entry. Re-asserting it is a separate call
  from this CDK change, because CFN will not correct the drift on its own: dev's synthesised value
  is unchanged by this edit (dev was already in the allowlist), so no changeset touches that
  resource. Restoring it needs an explicit `put-function-concurrency` or a forced update.
- **22 other Lambdas still omit `staging-b`** from their reserved-concurrency allowlist (23 of 27
  total; 14 of them in `services-stack.ts`). Deliberately left alone: fixing them all at once could
  re-hit the 100-unreserved floor that already broke the 2026-05-24 bootstrap, so it needs a costed
  pass rather than a sweep.
- **CI does not run the CDK jest tests at all.** `pr-validation.yml` runs `cdk synth --all --context
  env=dev` and nothing else — no job invokes jest under `infrastructure/cdk/`. So this test file and
  `api-gateway-throttle.test.ts` (#764) are useful locally but gate nothing in CI. Worth wiring up;
  note the suite needs `CDK_DOCKER_BUNDLING=1` because synthesising staging-b/staging/prod trips the
  secret-rotation-bouncer's deliberate anti-stub guard.
