## [2026-08-01] — CORRECTION + PR #738: the ECS zero-task dip is ~6 min on BOTH envs, and it self-heals

**This corrects the root-cause section of the entry below, published ~1 hour earlier.** The symptom and the fix location were right; the mechanism was wrong in two ways that matter operationally.

### What I got wrong
- I reported that the CDK deploy "scaled staging-b to zero and it stayed down until I recovered it." **It does not stay down.** Application Auto Scaling (`MinCapacity=1`) restores it, and on 2026-08-01 it had already recovered at **13:51** — my manual `update-service --desired-count 1` at ~13:57 was **redundant**.
- I reported it as a **staging-b-specific** fallthrough. **It is not.** `'dev'` misses `isStaging` too and takes the identical dip.

### What is actually true (measured, `DesiredTaskCount`, 1-min period)
| env | before | dip | recovered | at zero |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| staging-b | 13:44 → 1 | **13:45 → 0** | 13:51 → 1 | ~6 min |
| dev | 03:23 → 1 | **03:24 → 0** | 03:30 → 1 | ~6 min |

- Each window matches the `AgentEngineService` CFN `UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS → UPDATE_COMPLETE` span exactly. CloudFormation re-asserts the template's bootstrap `desiredCount: 0` on **every** update of the service resource.
- **Why only staging-b goes red:** `staging-b-promote` asserts `runningCount >= 1` at ~2.5 min — inside the dip — and that failure **skips the smoke matrix**, so the release ships unvalidated. Nothing samples dev in its window, so **dev has been taking the same ~6-minute outage silently on every deploy**.

### A second discarded hypothesis, recorded so it isn't re-run
"CFN pushes 0 because the template value changed" — also wrong: the line has never changed in git history, and *both* deployed templates already read `DesiredCount: 0`. What settled it was the CloudWatch series showing dev dipping identically, which ruled out any staging-b-specific cause. Reach for the metric on this one rather than reasoning from the template.

### Operational guidance (changed by the above)
- **Don't manual-scale** after a red promote — it self-heals in ~6 min.
- **Don't re-run the promote** for a green tick — it re-triggers the dip.
- The image + CDK content **has already landed** when that step fails; only smoke validation is missing.

### PR #738 (open, not merged)
- `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts:843` → declare **1** for staging-b, matching its autoscaling floor (1 not 3 — 3 would triple Fargate cost on a tier that has never needed it).
- **Only** the `desiredCount` expression changes. `isStaging` deliberately **not** redefined: it also drives `useCodeDeploy` (837) and a scheduled-scaling branch (975), so widening it would flip staging-b onto the CodeDeploy blue/green controller.
- **dev deliberately left at 0** — same dip, but its bootstrap case (fresh env, no ECR image) deserves its own decision.
- Verified by Docker-bundled synth: staging-b `DesiredCount: 1`, dev `DesiredCount: 0` unchanged; `tsc` clean.

## [2026-08-01] — Direction Setting: Phases 3–6 built (alignment, market data, plan/ROI, rehearsal)

Completes the code phases of the Direction Setting journey. With the 2026-07-31 entry below, **phases 1–6 of the implementation plan are built** — Phase 0 (the global blueprint library, 18h of human review) is deliberately not included, and Phase 4.1 (the O*NET commercial licence) is Bill's to obtain.

Branches pushed: `feat/direction-setting` (monorepo) and `feat/direction-setting-ui` (frontend). **No PR opened, nothing merged, nothing deployed, no migration applied.**

### Added
- **Stage 6 alignment, reusing Honor's evaluation engine as its second consumer.** The engine was built domain-neutral and had never had one; the seam was already an injectable kwarg, so this is `evaluate_fellow(..., config=DIRECTION_FIT_CONFIG)` and nothing under `app/honor/` changed. Archetypes are the nine role families Stage 3 already uses, so "align" speaks the same vocabulary as "explore".
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/tools/direction_setting/{alignment,direction_jobs}.py`
- **The async job path** (`202 → poll → 200`), copied from the dossier pattern including the non-obvious parts: the queued row written *before* the task is spawned, strong refs on in-flight tasks, every outcome persisted including failures. Used by stages 6, 9, 10 and the optional rehearsal narration.
- **`app/market/`** — a provider Protocol with a curated static dataset behind it. `WageRange` is a frozen dataclass with five required fields and no defaults, so a point estimate is structurally inexpressible.
- **The close-the-gap plan and job ROI.**
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/tools/direction_setting/{plan,roi}.py`
- **Candidate-owned rehearsal** — a real phase machine, DB-backed, resumable, 90-day rolling retention.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/tools/direction_setting/rehearsal.py`, `alembic/versions/025_create_direction_rehearsal.py`, `services/migration-runner/migrations/direction_rehearsal.sql`
- **Journey export** in all 8 docgen formats. Every one of the 13 stages appears whether or not it has an artefact — people download this half-finished, and a section silently omitted would mislead them about how much is real.
- **Frontend surfaces** for alignment, salary, plan/ROI and rehearsal, all wired to the above.

### Fixed
- **GRANT's invented salary fallback is retired.** `_FALLBACK = (55_000, 38_000, 4)` was returned for *any* occupation outside its 20 rows — and `GrantLoansPage` divides projected loan payments by `entryLevelSalary` for debt-to-income, so every student researching an occupation outside that table had their ratio computed against a fabricated $38,000. Unknown now returns absent. The retired tuple is named by value in the test file so its return would be caught by name.
- **A load-sensitive test flake.** `test_alignment`'s drain helper gave the worker a fixed 2s of wall clock — enough on an idle machine, not always on a busy one. It now awaits the actual in-flight task: 5/5 clean runs, suite time down to 1.3s.
- **The CI allowlist entries added in Phase 1 were wrong.** Three named files never existed and three real suites (`test_report`, `test_plan`, `test_roi`) were absent. Since agent-engine's `pr-validation` probes with `[ -f ... ]`, a missing file is skipped *silently* — those suites gated nothing. This is exactly the trap item 1.7 exists to prevent, and it caught itself.

### Notable design decisions
- **Behavioural gaps can never carry a cost**, enforced structurally at four layers rather than by convention: the constructor raises, there are two item classes (`BehaviouralItem` has no `cost` attribute at all), the serialised row omits the key rather than sending null, and the cost total selects by `isinstance` so a behavioural item is never *offered* to it. Pricing one would fabricate the ROI's central number.
- **The ROI refuses, and refusing is the ordinary path.** Eight named refusal conditions. Partial pricing emits the arithmetic as a declared *floor* and still reports what is missing. Figures are a band across three wage points — there is deliberately no scalar payback key.
- **Confidence degradation is a ledger, not a footnote**, sized so no ROI on the current static table can reach the `high` band.
- **Rehearsal feedback contains no score, grade, or digit.** That is the testable form of "don't rebuild Maven" — which is manager-gated, evaluative, and whose phase enum turned out to be inert in production.
- **A goal→area mapping bug found in Honor.** `_map_goal_to_area` uses an unanchored substring test, so *"a career in tech"* maps to **People & Care** because "care" is inside "career". Rather than edit Honor, a whole-word confirmation is applied on the Direction Setting side; it can only reject a proposal, never invent one.

### Verification
- **Backend: 1127 tests pass** across `direction_setting` (327), `grant`, `honor` and `lumen` — the new vertical regressed none of the existing three.
- **Frontend: 4091 tests / 522 suites**, CI coverage gate met, `npm run build` green.
- **Not verified:** nothing deployed, no browser check, migrations `002` / `024` / `025` unapplied, and no path exercised against real user data.

## [2026-08-01] — Agent Engine: scale on in-flight LLM calls, not CPU

### Fixed
- **ECS autoscaling could no longer detect saturation.** CPU target-tracking at 70%
  (`agent-engine-stack.ts`) was a working signal only while the Anthropic client was
  synchronous — a blocked worker pinned a thread, so load showed up as CPU. After the async
  swap (PR #735) a task can hold hundreds of concurrent in-flight LLM calls while burning
  almost no CPU, so the service would saturate *silently*: turn latency climbing and jobs
  queueing behind the DB pool while the autoscaler saw an idle fleet and never added a task.
  - **New primary policy** `InFlightLlmCallsScaling` — target-tracks a custom metric the app
    now publishes. Scale out fast (60s), scale in slow (5m).
  - **New backstop** `RequestCountScaling` on `ALBRequestCountPerTarget` for load the gauge
    can't see (plain REST + the `/chat/jobs` poll storm). Rolling-deploy path only — the
    CODE_DEPLOY path swaps target groups per deployment, so binding to the blue group there
    would break the moment traffic shifted to green.
  - **CPU + memory policies KEPT** as safety nets for genuine compute pressure.
  - **New saturation alarm** — target tracking goes quiet once already at maxCapacity (it
    keeps wanting tasks and does nothing); the alarm names the next constraints in order.
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts`, `lib/config.ts`
    (+`inFlightLlmCallsTarget`, `+requestsPerTargetTarget`; dev 10/worker, staging-b 12,
    default 25).

### Added
- **`app/observability/saturation.py`** — in-flight gauge (`track_llm_call`) + a background
  reporter publishing `InFlightLLMCalls` / `PeakInFlightLLMCalls` / `InFlightChatJobs` every
  30s to `InspireGenius/AgentEngine`. Wired into `provider.chat()` and `provider.stream()`
  (the stream is counted for the whole generator lifetime, not just the request) and started
  from the app lifespan.
- **10 app tests** (`tests/test_saturation_gauge.py`) + **7 CDK template assertions**
  (`infrastructure/cdk/test/agent-engine-scaling.test.ts` — the repo's first real CDK test;
  the existing `test/cdk.test.ts` was a commented-out stub).

### Two design points established by measurement, not by reading code
Both invalidated the obvious implementation:
1. **Track the PEAK per interval, not the instantaneous gauge.** Sampling every 30s against
   ~11s turns systematically misses bursts — a real burst of **7** concurrent calls registered
   as a 1-minute Average of **0.167** because every sample landed between waves. Target-tracking
   that number would under-react to exactly the load it exists to catch.
2. **The publisher is a WORKER, not a task.** uvicorn runs `--workers 2` and each worker runs
   its own reporter, so one task emits 2 datapoints per interval (confirmed: `SampleCount` 4/min
   for a single task). The Average is a per-worker mean; the target is calibrated per worker
   (dev 10 ⇒ ~20 concurrent turns per task).

### Verified (metric live on dev; the policy lands on the next CDK deploy)
- Sustained 15-concurrent load = ~7.5 per worker → metric read **7.75**. Tracks reality.
- Idle → **0.0 on every tick**, so scale-in is never starved of data.
- A transient 30-turn burst read 7.5 avg / 16 max and correctly did **not** cross the target
  of 10 — a 21s spike that ends long before a task can boot should not earn permanent capacity.
- CDK: `tsc` clean; 7/7 template assertions pass. Full-app `cdk synth` is blocked locally by
  the trainer-stack `ig-auth` pip/cffi bundling (the known local-bundling trap) — the focused
  `Template.fromStack(AgentEngineStack)` test sidesteps it, and CI runs `cdk synth --all`.
- **NOT verified:** an actual scale-out event. The policy does not exist in AWS until a CDK
  deploy, which was deliberately not run locally (local deploys re-bundle and can clobber the
  stack's Lambdas).

### Incident noted during this work
- Dev agent-engine went to `desiredCount=0` at 23:23 EDT via CloudFormation while PR #733 was
  being deployed by CI; dev chat was 503 until restored to 1 task. The live scalable target read
  `MinCapacity: 0` even though `config.ts` says `staticMin: 1`.
  **CORRECTION (2026-08-01):** this was first written up as "the deployed CDK is stale relative to
  config". That was wrong — the deployed CFN template says `MinCapacity: 1`. The real cause is the
  CI roll job in `.github/workflows/agent-engine-image.yml`, which lifted min to 1 for the deploy
  window and then restored it to a **hardcoded 0**, leaving dev's floor at 0 after every merge to
  `development`. Root-caused and fixed in **PR #737**; see the 2026-08-01 entry.
- This branch was rebased onto `development` (43104e5d, #733) mid-session after discovering
  that pushing `:latest` from an unmerged branch had overwritten CI's `dev-43104e5` image.

## [2026-08-01] — CI: agent-engine roll must restore the floor it found, not a hardcoded 0

### Fixed
- **Every merge to `development` permanently dropped dev's ECS autoscaling floor to 0.** The
  `roll-ecs-dev` job in `.github/workflows/agent-engine-image.yml` lifted `min-capacity` to 1 for
  the deploy window, then restored it to a **hardcoded 0**. That job is the last writer —
  CloudFormation only reasserts `MinCapacity` on a stack *update* — so dev was left unable to
  recover from a scale-to-zero after every deploy. This is what left dev chat 503'ing on
  2026-07-31 23:23 EDT when a CFN update took `desiredCount` to 0 during #733's deploy.
  - The step's own comments justified the 0 with two claims that **stopped being true on
    2026-07-19**, when dev moved to always-on (`scheduledScalingEnabled: false`, `staticMin: 1`):
    *"off-hours scheduled scaling sets min=0 on dev"* (there are now **zero** scheduled actions on
    the target) and *"schedule cron will reassert its own min on next firing"* (there is no cron).
  - **The job can no longer author a permanent change:** capture current min/max; skip the lift
    entirely when the floor is already ≥ 1 (the normal case now, so nothing to restore); when a
    lift IS needed restore exactly the captured bounds, so a deliberate `--min-capacity 0`
    (e.g. `/agent-stop`) still survives a deploy; stop hardcoding `--max-capacity 4`; skip cleanly
    when no scalable target exists instead of aborting on a non-numeric `MinCapacity`.
  - PR **#737**.

### Correction to the 2026-08-01 scaling entry
- That entry (and the #736 PR body) first attributed the `MinCapacity` mismatch to *"the deployed
  CDK is stale relative to config"*. **That was wrong.** The deployed CFN template says
  `MinCapacity: 1`; the live target read `0`. The cause was the CI roll job above, not stale
  infrastructure. Diagnosed by reading the deployed template, confirming zero scheduled actions,
  and then CloudTrail: **10 consecutive deploys** since 2026-07-27, each a `min=1` lift followed
  ~3 minutes later by a `min=0` restore, all from `gha-agent-engine-roll-*`.

### Refinement from PR #738 (landed same day, another terminal)
- #738 found the **other half** of the 2026-07-31 outage and it is the more direct cause: the ECS
  service declared `desiredCount: isProd ? 5 : isStaging ? 3 : 0`, and since `isStaging` is
  `envName === 'staging'`, **both dev and staging-b inherited that bootstrap `0`** — which
  CloudFormation re-asserts on *every* service update, making each deploy a ~6-minute outage.
- That means **#737 alone would not have prevented the 503.** As #738 notes, a `MinCapacity=1`
  scalable target does not rescue a service at 0 tasks: target tracking reacts to utilization
  alarms, and 0 tasks emit no utilization. #737 stops the floor being left at 0 permanently
  (config drift, and it misrepresents the env's declared intent); #738 stops the outage at source.
  Both were needed; neither is sufficient alone. Earlier wording here that implied #737 fixed the
  outage overstated it.

### Verified
- Live dev scalable target corrected to `min=1, max=4` (matches the deployed CFN template).
- Workflow bash exercised against a mocked AWS CLI across `min=0` / `min=1` / `min=2` / `None` /
  empty — **only** the `min=0` case lifts; every other case is a no-op.
- **NOT verified end-to-end:** the workflow runs from `development`, so the new logic can only be
  exercised once #737 merges. The next roll should log
  `Floor already >= 1 — no lift needed, nothing to restore.`

### Housekeeping
- PR **#735 closed** as superseded by **#736** (#735 rebased onto #733 + the autoscaling work;
  the async-client commits are content-identical).
- Note for future sessions: the roll workflow's own header documents that PR builds **never** push
  `:latest`, citing a 2026-05-11 regression where a pre-merge feature-branch image took the tag.
  A manual `docker push :latest` bypasses that guard — which is exactly what happened during the
  #736 work and required a rebase + rebuild to undo.

### Defect found by the promote — the new policy was inert on staging-b
- Post-promote verification showed staging-b publishing its CloudWatch dimension as **`Environment=dev`**.
  Cause: **nothing has ever set `AGENT_ENGINE_ENVIRONMENT`**, in any environment, so

### CORRECTION — why the staging-b concurrency probe could not run
- This entry originally said `[email redacted]` "does not exist in staging-b's user table". **That was
  wrong**, and it was inferred from an API error message rather than checked. The account is present and
  healthy: `user_id=[uuid]`, `is_active=t`, `is_deleted=f`,
  `is_email_verified=t`, `auth_provider=cognito`, with a `user_entitlements` row.
- The real reason: **`POST /v1/magic-auth` is deliberately DISABLED on staging-b**
  (`settings.magic_auth_enabled=False`) because it "hands out a valid session from an email alone", and
  when disabled it returns `message="Not found"` specifically to hide the endpoint. The handler
  distinguishes the two cases precisely — disabled endpoint → `"Not found"`, missing user →

  (`services/auth-service/app/routes/magic_auth.py`).
- So a staging-b token needs the real Cognito login, or the emailed magic-LINK flow
  (`/v1/magic-link/request` → `/verify`, which is independent of that gate and enabled). Neither is
  something to route around: the gate exists precisely to stop sessions being minted from an email.

## [2026-08-01] — PRISM: wrong colour scores + "Orange", duplicated TTS read-back, slow prompt injection

Five reported defects. Every diagnosis below was confirmed against real dev data or a failing test — none inferred.

### Fixed — Red was being reported as "Orange" (there is no Orange in PRISM)
PRISM has four colours: **Gold, Green, Blue, Red**. "Orange" survives only as the name of the legacy `prism_results.orange` DB column. That name was leaking into the model's own context two ways: the injected `<prism_profile>` block emitted `<orange>`, and Aura's system prompt said verbatim *"Treat Red and Orange as synonyms; mirror the user's wording."* The model was doing what it was told.
- Inject block now emits `<red>`; the DB column keeps its name (no migration, no benefit to renaming).
- Aura's **and** Meridian's prompts now forbid the word as a colour name outright, and instruct answering in "Red" even when the user says "Orange".
- Reference text no longer offers it as an alias: `prism_knowledge`, `disc_knowledge`, `enneagram_knowledge`, `reconciliation`, `prism_parser`, `report_import`.
- `prism_canon.normalise_colour_names()` is a last-resort guard applied to Meridian's response. Scoped deliberately narrowly — it rewrites "Orange" only in PRISM contexts (adjacent to a quadrant noun, to Focusing/Delivering, or in a colour list) so ordinary prose ("orange juice", "an orange dress") is untouched. It also fixes the article, since "an Orange quadrant" would otherwise become "an Red quadrant".
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/prism_canon.py`, `app/llm/prompts.py`, `app/memory/integration.py`, `app/agents/meridian.py`, `app/agents/coaching/prism_knowledge.py`

### Fixed — the Blue score was wrong, and so were Gold and Red
Each colour is the mean of the two behaviours in its quadrant, but the pairing was **rotated** against the licensed PRISM manual. Confirmed arithmetically against dev assessment `4f1066ba` (Innovating 88, Initiating 13, Supporting 92, Coordinating 80, Focusing 32, Delivering 46, Finishing 60, Evaluating 96):

| Colour | Stored | Correct | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Green | 50.5 | (88+13)/2 = **50.5** | correct |
| **Blue** | **78.0** | (92+80)/2 = **86.0** | was Gold's pair |
| Gold | 39.0 | (60+96)/2 = **78.0** | was Red's pair |
| Red | 86.0 | (32+46)/2 = **39.0** | was Blue's pair |

Only Green was right — its pair is identical under both groupings, which is why the error survived. The row's own `raw_data.color_derivation` recorded the wrong pairing in plain text. **The user reported Blue; three of the four colours were affected.**

The rotation lived in four places (storage, Aura's radar, the frontend colours, and a one-time backfill) and was documented in-code as *"a pre-existing, deliberately-unfixed quadrant-mapping inconsistency."* All now derive from one dependency-free source of truth.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/prism_canon.py`, `app/memory/long_term.py`, `app/agents/coaching/prism_agent.py`, `app/agents/coaching/frameworks/reconciliation.py`, `inspire-genius-frontend/src/constants/prism.ts`

### Fixed — stored rows corrected with no data migration
`get_latest_prism` derives colours at **read time** from the authoritative `assessment_scores` rows, so fixing the mapping corrected every user with an assessment immediately (all 10 on dev). Legacy `prism_results` rows are repaired on read from `raw_data.dimensions` when present, and log when they are. No `UPDATE` was run against user data.

### Fixed — "scores get misrepresented at times"
The read was already per-turn and uncached, and `SharedContext` is per-request, so staleness was not the mechanism. The real hazard was **absence**: memory sections render in priority order (corrections → goals → PRISM → …), each gated on remaining token budget, so enough corrections or goals silently pushed the entire `<prism_profile>` block out of context. With no scores present the model falls back to numbers from earlier in the conversation — indistinguishable, to the user, from a stale score. The block's cost is now reserved before the variable-length sections.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/memory/integration.py`

### Fixed — Meridian read responses back twice
Reported as *"once completely from start to finish, other times repeating paragraphs and sentences."* Both symptoms are the same bug. `speakText` had no re-entrancy protection: it replaced `ttsAbortRef` with a fresh controller **without aborting the previous one** and reset the cancelled flag, so a second call for the same turn left the first run's in-flight sentence requests resolving into the audio queue — a plain FIFO with no dedupe. Two clean runs read the whole answer twice; two overlapping runs interleave and repeat fragments. A settled turn can reach TTS from more than one delivery path (async-job settlement and the WS `complete` frame), which is what triggered it.
- Dedupe on content, so one turn is spoken at most once.
- Genuinely abort a previous run when different text arrives.
- The streaming-TTS path records what it spoke — gated on whether it *actually ran*, since muting creates no controller and suppressing the fallback would have produced silence instead of a duplicate.

Verified non-vacuous: with the guard removed the test fails with both sentences synthesized twice, in order.
  - Files: `inspire-genius-frontend/src/pages/user/MeridianChat.tsx`

### Fixed — injected questions were slow and displayed raw scaffolding
The warm-up `GET /v1/agents/health` and the auto-send fired in the **same tick**, so a question injected from another surface got zero warm-up window and hit a cold ECS task — paying API Gateway's 30s cap and then `startJob`'s 3s/6s retry backoff before the job was even accepted. A typed question never pays this, because the user's typing time *is* the warm-up window. That is the entire gap between "typed here" and "arrived from elsewhere". The dispatch now waits for the health ping (sub-second when warm, capped at 8s so a hung ping can never strand a question); bubbles still render immediately, so there is no blank screen.

Separately, Lumen sends `question + scope line` as the prompt and the whole composed string was rendered as the user's own message. `prefillDisplay` / `autoSendDisplayText` lets the full prompt reach the model while the bubble shows only what the person asked.
  - Files: `inspire-genius-frontend/src/pages/user/MeridianChat.tsx`, `src/components/user/chat/ChatWindow.tsx`, `src/types/chat/component-types.ts`, `src/pages/lumen/CoachingPage.tsx`

### Verification
- Agent engine: **+29 tests**; full suite 4264 passed. The 167 failures are pre-existing (no OpenAI key / AWS credentials locally) — failure sets diffed against `origin/development` and found **byte-identical**, so zero regressions.
- Frontend: **+8 tests**; full suite under CI's exact coverage gate (`54/55/55/55`) — **520 suites / 3986 tests, exit 0**. `npm run build` (tsc + vite) clean.
- The token-budget test asserts the budget was genuinely exhausted first, so it cannot pass vacuously.
- PRs: monorepo **#743**, frontend **#327**.

## [2026-08-01] — PRISM colour guard: don't rewrite "Orange" when the model is saying it isn't a colour

Follow-up to the same-day PRISM fix (#743). **Found by an adversarial probe against deployed dev, not by a test.**

### Fixed
Asked *"Am I an Orange? What does my Orange score mean?"* — the case most likely to defeat the fix — Meridian correctly replied:

> "Your quadrant is called **Red** in PRISM — there is no **Orange** colour in the framework."

The `normalise_colour_names` output guard then rewrote that second "Orange" (it was followed by "colour", one of the quadrant-noun contexts) and what actually reached the user was:

> "…there is no **Red** colour in the framework."

Self-contradicting nonsense, in precisely the situation the guard exists to serve: the user uses the wrong term and the model explains that it isn't real.

The guard now skips a match preceded within 60 characters by a negation cue (`no` / `not` / `never` / `isn't` / `rather than` / `instead of`). The window is deliberately bounded so a negation in an earlier clause cannot disable a legitimate rewrite later in the same response — there is a test for exactly that.

- **+9 tests**, including the verbatim sentence from production.
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/prism_canon.py`, `tests/test_prism_canon.py`
- PR **#746**, merged `7af79c3e`.

### Everything else in that probe was correct
Red 34 (Focusing 7 / Delivering 61), Blue 92, Green 91.5, Gold 52 — all matching the corrected derivation — and the word "Orange" appeared nowhere else despite the user using it four times.

### Standing lesson
Any regex that rewrites LLM output will eventually corrupt a *correct* sentence. Probe the adversarial case (user uses the wrong term, model explains why it's wrong), not just the happy path. The prompts and the injected `<prism_profile>` block are what actually stop the model saying "Orange"; this guard is only drift insurance and must never damage good output while doing its job.

## [2026-08-01] — PRISM Brain Map diagram, and the Underlying-vs-Consistent score-type comparison

Two pieces: a diagram emitted whenever a turn reports the user's own scores, and a read-only comparison of the two PRISM score maps for every dev user.

### Added — PRISM Brain Map, emitted with any turn that reports the user's scores
The four colour scores were only ever delivered as prose. They now arrive as the canonical map, with labels and scores.

**The layout is not a free choice** — it comes from the licensed reference text in `prism_knowledge` (`AXES_DISCERNING_DYNAMIC`): *"The top left of the PRISM map is the Gold quadrant … the bottom right is Blue … The top right … is Green … the bottom left is Red."*

Two things a naive 2×2 gets wrong, both now encoded **and asserted against the rendered SVG geometry** so a future edit cannot quietly rotate it the way the score pairing was:
- **The axes are DIAGONALS**, not the grid lines. Gold + Blue share "less powerful" (Discerning); Green + Red share "more powerful" (Dynamic).
- **Opposites mirror HORIZONTALLY**, not through the centre — they *"apply across the Gold/Green colour quadrants and the Red/Blue colour quadrants"*. Evaluating faces Initiating, Finishing faces Innovating, Focusing faces Supporting, Delivering faces Co-Ordinating; each panel's rows are ordered to put them literally opposite one another.

**Delivered in `metadata["prism_map"]`, never in the response text.** TTS synthesises `content`; an inline SVG there would be read aloud as markup — the exact failure mode removed earlier the same day. A markdown table and a one-line description carry identical numbers for TTS, screen readers and plain-text export.

**When it fires:** "each time scores are requested" is deliberately *not* every PRISM turn — a map on *"what does high Focusing mean?"* is clutter. Primary signal is that the answer **actually quotes at least two of the user's four colour scores** (self-correcting, no keyword vocabulary to maintain); an explicit *"show me my profile"* is a second trigger. Number matching is boundary-guarded so `52` does not match `1952`.

**A bug this nearly shipped with:** the first implementation read `context.metadata["prism_scores"]` — as several existing call sites do. **That key is never populated** on the REST or WS chat paths (metadata carries only `file_ids` / `system_prompt_override` / `user_profile_block`), so the map would have silently never rendered. Scores now come from the memory manager, behind a cheap no-DB pre-check so an ordinary turn adds no query.

**Frontend:** rendered through a **data-URI `<img>`, not `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`** — the markup is server-generated and asserted script-free, but an `<img>` cannot execute script under any circumstance. `encodeURIComponent` not `btoa` (the map contains `↔` and `·`). `alt` is the full numeric read-out so screen readers get data, not "image", with a "Show the numbers" toggle. `buildTurnHtml` gained an optional `figure` field rather than smuggling markup through the escaped markdown `body`; a test asserts the body is still escaped when a figure is present.

- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/prism_map.py`, `app/agents/meridian.py`, `inspire-genius-frontend/src/components/prism/PrismMapFigure.tsx`, `src/components/user/chat/ChatWindowChatTab.tsx`, `src/lib/exportTranscript/exportTurn.ts`, `src/pages/user/MeridianChat.tsx`, `src/types/chat/data-types.ts`, `src/hooks/agents/useMeridianWebSocket.ts`
- PRs: mono **#755**, FE **#332**

**Render-verified, not just unit-tested.** The SVG was rasterised and inspected: the first version placed the axis captions on top of the panel borders, illegible — completely invisible in the source. Moved to a footer legend and re-checked.

### Reported (no change made) — Underlying vs Consistent, all 14 dev users
PRISM measures each behaviour three times: **Underlying** (instinctive), **Adapted** (environment-modified), **Consistent** (the manual's "likely overall behaviour" / "normal" preferences). The platform derives every colour score from **`Underlying`** only — a pre-existing choice, hardcoded as `SCORE_TYPE = "Underlying"`.

Read-only comparison across all 14 dev users with an authoritative PRISM assessment:
- **52 of 56 colour scores would change** under `Consistent`
- mean shift **8.5** points, max **22.0**
- **25 intensity-band changes**
- movement is almost entirely **downward**

**The consequence that matters:** many scores drop out of the **≥75 overdone-strength band**, which drives specific coaching language. User `3468e498` shows Green 91.5 / Blue 92 under `Underlying` (both flagged overdone) versus 74 / 72.5 under `Consistent` — just below threshold, so those warnings would disappear entirely.

**Nothing was changed.** Switching the score type would silently move every number for every user; that is a product decision for Bill or a PRISM-accredited practitioner, not an inference. Tooling: `scratchpad/compare_score_types.py` (SELECT only).

**Incidental finding:** six dev users share byte-identical scores (78 / 50.5 / 86 / 39) — almost certainly duplicated test data, worth a look independently of this decision.

**Also learned:** the migration-runner Lambda truncates result sets at **10 rows**. Earlier queries in this session looked complete but were silently cut off. Aggregate into a single `json_agg` row when pulling anything larger.

### Verification
- Agent engine: **+31 tests**; full suite 4305 passed; failure set **byte-identical** to `origin/development` (167 pre-existing, no API keys locally) → zero regressions. One run showed 168 — a flaky test; two re-runs and a clean-baseline diff agree at 167.
- Frontend: **+12 tests**; full suite under CI's exact coverage gate (`54/55/55/55`) — **529 suites / 4171 tests, exit 0**; `npm run build` clean.

Between scoping the promote and creating the tag, another terminal merged **#750**, so the first tag silently contained a feature that had not been assessed. ## [2026-07-31] — Fix: the dead `job_complete` WebSocket push (PR #733)

Implements the fix for the defect diagnosed in the entry below. **Code complete, CI green (32/32), NOT yet merged or deployed** — the merge is awaiting Bill's approval.

### Fixed
- **`push_to_user()` can now reach a browser.** It walked `_user_sessions`, an in-memory dict of native FastAPI sockets held by the ECS task; a browser's socket terminates at API Gateway → ws-proxy, so the task never held it and the push returned 0 on every call in every deployed environment.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/websocket/remote_push.py` (new), `services/agent-engine/app/websocket/manager.py`
- **The silence that hid it.** Success logged INFO, an exception logged DEBUG, and `delivered == 0` hit neither — so a permanently broken push wrote no log line at all. The count is now logged unconditionally, and a test asserts `if delivered:` never comes back.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/main.py`, `services/agent-engine/tests/test_ws_remote_push.py`

### Added
- `userId-index` GSI (KEYS_ONLY) on the ws-connections table; ECS task role granted read + `DeleteItem` on the table and `execute-api:ManageConnections` on the WS API; container gets `AGENT_ENGINE_WS_CONNECTIONS_TABLE` + `AGENT_ENGINE_APIGW_WS_ENDPOINT`.
  - Files: `infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts`
- Settings `ws_connections_table`, `apigw_ws_endpoint`, `ws_remote_push_enabled` (runtime kill switch).
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/config.py`
- 17 tests, added to the pr-validation allowlist so they actually gate.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/tests/test_ws_remote_push.py`, `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml`

### Design notes
- **Reuses the existing registry rather than adding a second one** — ws-proxy already writes `connectionId -> userId` on `$connect`. Only the index, the IAM and the transport were missing.
- **No frontend change needed**: `useMeridianJob` already settles on a `job_complete` frame and cancels the poll. The client has been waiting for a frame that never came.
- **Blast radius contained**: the job row is committed *before* the push is attempted, so every failure path returns 0 rather than raising — a broken push costs latency, not data. Unconfigured is a silent no-op.

### Verification
- **17 new tests pass; 3 fail against the pre-fix baseline** (verified by stashing the source and re-running), so they catch the bug rather than passing by construction. The other 14 cover genuinely new surface.
- **Zero new failures**: 26 failed / 187 passed with the change vs 26 failed / 170 passed on the stashed baseline — failure sets byte-identical via `comm`. Those 26 are the known `test_websocket.py` global-state leak (existing P3).
- **`cdk diff` vs live dev**: the GSI is an **in-place** table update, NOT a replacement; the TaskDefinition "replacement" is just a new revision.
- **Identity alignment checked against live data** — a mismatch would have made the fix silently do nothing. ws-proxy stores the Cognito `sub`, `chat_async` uses `claims["sub"]`, and the 7 live staging-b rows carry real `sub` UUIDs rather than the `"unvalidated"` degradation value.

### Separate bug found, NOT fixed
- `services/ws-proxy/handler.py` hardcodes `FunctionName="ig-dev-ws-forwarder"`. **That Lambda does not exist on staging-b** and is in the CDK on neither env — undocumented drift. The WS *chat* path is therefore dead on staging-b (chat works there only because the UI uses the async-jobs REST path). Reported, not fixed; out of scope for this PR.

## [2026-07-31] — Agent Engine: async Anthropic client (per-worker turn ceiling removed)

### Fixed
- **`AnthropicDirectProvider` blocked the uvicorn event loop on every LLM call.** The provider
  built a **sync** `anthropic.Anthropic` client and called `client.messages.create(...)` /
  `client.messages.stream(...)` inline inside `async def chat` / `async def stream`. The sync
  client blocks the calling thread for the whole HTTP round-trip, so each Meridian turn froze
  its worker's event loop for the full LLM call (~20s post-#724). With `--workers 2` in the
  Dockerfile CMD this capped an ECS task at **2 concurrent turns** no matter how many tasks
  ran — and while a turn was pending, nothing else on that worker was scheduled: not other
  users' `/v1/agents/chat/jobs/{id}` polls, not the ALB health check on `/v1/agents/health`.
  - Swapped to `anthropic.AsyncAnthropic` + `await`. `_get_client()` keys the client to the
    running event loop so a process with several loops (or tests calling `asyncio.run` more
    than once) rebuilds instead of reusing a client bound to a dead loop; an externally
    injected client (`provider._client = ...` in tests) is never replaced.
  - `stream()` moved to `async with` / `async for` + `await stream.get_final_message()`.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/llm/provider.py`
  - PR #735 (branch `perf/agent-engine-async-llm-provider`), **merged: not yet**.

### Added
- **`scripts/loadtest_provider_concurrency.py`** — measures whether the ceiling actually moves.
  `stub` mode (default) drives the real provider against a stub alongside a faithful
  reproduction of the old sync path; no network, no LLM spend, no blast radius on the shared
  Anthropic org quota. `live --url ... --token ...` fires N concurrent `/v1/agents/chat/async`
  submissions at a deployed engine and polls each to completion (real spend — keep N small).
- **`tests/test_provider_async_concurrency.py`** — 3 tests: N concurrent calls overlap rather
  than serialize, the event loop stays responsive while a call is pending, and the loop guard
  does not discard an injected client.

### Changed
- `tests/test_provider_temperature.py` fakes and two `tests/test_prism_agent.py` stubs were
  sync-shaped (`def create`, `__enter__`/`__exit__`); now async to match the client.

### Verified
- **Stub load test** (real provider vs reproduced old path):
  `before  in-flight=1/250, wall=10.69s, loop-ticks=0` →
  `after   in-flight=250/250, wall=0.05s, loop-ticks=18`.
  `loop-ticks=0` is the production symptom — a heartbeat coroutine never got scheduled at all.
- **Deployed to dev** (image `ig-dev-agent-engine:asyncllm` = `:latest`,
  digest `sha256:a98a8632…`; ECS rollout COMPLETED; ECS-exec confirmed the running task
  carries `AsyncAnthropic` + both awaited call sites).
- **Real-traffic smoke on dev**: 8 concurrent turns, 1 task / 2 workers → **8/8 complete in
  12.5s wall-clock** (slowest single turn 12.5s). Pre-fix that is 4 sequential waves of 2, ≥44s.
- **Test-suite delta vs `origin/development`: zero regressions.** The agent-engine suite is
  already red on development (167 failures — they need an OpenAI key). Before: 167 failed /
  3877 passed. After: 167 failed / 3880 passed. Failure sets byte-identical; +3 = the new tests.
- Rollback: dev `latest` was `sha256:aed23120…` (pushed 2026-07-30 23:56) before this deploy.

### Not changed (deliberate)
- `app/quality/scorer.py` and `app/corrections/lookup.py` have the same sync-client-in-`async
  def` shape but **no callers anywhere in `app/`** — dead code, off the request path.

### Follow-ups exposed (NOT in this PR)
- **ECS autoscaling is CPU-at-70%** (`infrastructure/cdk/lib/agent-engine-stack.ts:709`). A
  worker holding N idle HTTP waits burns ~no CPU, so the service now saturates *without ever
  scaling out*. Wants ALB request-count or `chat_jobs` queue-depth scaling.
- **DB pool / Aurora are the next ceilings** — `app/db.py` (pool 10 + overflow 20) and
  `app/memory/database.py` (5 + 10) per worker; staging-b Aurora is capped at 0.5–2.0 ACU
  (~450 connections), dev at 0.5–8.0.
- **No retry/backoff on Anthropic 429s**, which higher real concurrency now makes reachable.

## [2026-07-30] — Meridian latency: OUTCOME ~60s → ~20s (browser-confirmed) + the dead WebSocket push

Closing entry for the latency work logged in the three entries below (build, merge+dev verification, staging-b promote).

### Outcome
- **Bill confirmed time-to-response is now ~20 seconds, down from the ~60 seconds that opened the work** — a real turn in the real UI on his own workload. This is the first *like-for-like* measurement: every earlier number came from CloudWatch traces where the question, the answering agent and the input size all differed, and those were explicitly NOT presented as a controlled comparison.

### Found while explaining the remaining headroom — the `job_complete` WebSocket push is DEAD BY CONSTRUCTION
- `_run_chat_job` pushes a `job_complete` frame so a connected client renders immediately instead of waiting for the next poll; the frontend has the matching `notifyPushFrame` short-circuit. **It has never fired.**
- `push_to_user()` resolves recipients from `self._user_sessions` — an **in-memory dict of native FastAPI sockets held by that ECS task**. In production the browser's socket terminates at **API Gateway → ws-proxy Lambda**, never at the task, so the dict is always empty and the function returns `0`.
- **It fails silently:** the call site logs on success and logs at `DEBUG` on exception, but `delivered == 0` is neither — so the failure path emits nothing at all.
- Confirmed four ways: zero hits for `"pushed completion"` across 3 days of staging-b logs; no `execute-api:ManageConnections` on the ECS task role (granted only to the ws-proxy Lambda, `agent-engine-stack.ts:1454`); `APIGW_WS_ENDPOINT` absent from the entire CDK; and the correct `LambdaConnectionManager` class exists but its docstring scopes it to "the Lambda deployment path".
- **Consequence:** delivery is entirely the 2s poll (`useMeridianJob.ts:213`), costing 0–2s per turn — and far more in a backgrounded tab, where Chrome throttles `setInterval` to ~1/min. That is likely part of why 60s was observed while logs showed 49s.
- **This corrected an earlier claim made in the same session** that the completion fetch was push-triggered; that had been inferred from a poll landing 67ms after an LLM call, which was coincidence.

### Answered: fixing it will NOT add latency
- Both call sites (`main.py:1203` job_error, `main.py:1268` job_complete) run **after** the terminal `update_status`, i.e. after the answer is already fetchable. The push sits off the user-visible path inside the background task, so the fix adds ~10–50ms to that task and *subtracts* the 0–2s poll wait. **Implementation caveat recorded: keep the push after the status write and keep it best-effort** — moving it earlier or making it blocking would put an external API call on the critical path.

### Remaining headroom, deliberately deferred
- Parallelise the ~4–5s preamble (two SERIAL haiku calls + three embedding round-trips before the answer LLM starts).
- Prompt-cache the 30,491-char attached document (~2s + a large share of the token bill); it sits in the DYNAMIC block after the cache breakpoint.
- SSE streaming stays OFF — progressive delivery over polling got most of the win without the API Gateway 30s-cap exposure.
- Fix the WebSocket channel (~4–6 CC / 6–10 h), which also repairs `job_complete`.
- Two broken staging-b tables: `response_decision_rules` missing; RLHF `ModelRouter` DynamoDB table not found.

PR #725 merged (`c7c2e7f5`). Follow-up PR #726 open.

### Deployed
- **dev** — `cdk-deploy` run `30586572441`, all 5 jobs green including the
  stub-zip detector and the RAG post-deploy probes. Lambda `ig-dev-document-service`
  `CodeSha256` moved `n1OCpyPP…` → `8Yz3ssfB…` at 22:40:13Z.

  `30588239124`, all 6 jobs green including the authenticated smoke matrix. Lambda
  `ig-staging-b-document-service` `CodeSha256` moved `tDSuqnGM…` → `3rbfqDiJ…` at
  22:58:48Z. Carried **only** #725 — another terminal had promoted #724 half an hour
  earlier under `release-stable-2026-07-30-meridian-latency`. No migrations.

### Verified against the deployed artifact, not the exit code
A green pipeline and a changed `CodeSha256` prove *something* deployed, not that the
fix works. The deployed Lambda logs at WARNING, so the new bail-out `logger.info` is
invisible — that probe couldn't discriminate old code from new. Used the behaviour
instead: re-drove one stranded document and watched it cross the exact boundary the
bug sat on. Under the old code the skip-set would have discarded the request.
- dev `csv_data_Lee_Allen.csv`: `failed chunks=0 text=0` → `ready chunks=14 text=6249`

|---|---|---|

| dev | 139 ready / 14 failed | **152 ready / 1 failed** |

The remaining dev row is `my_resume.pdf` — **no S3 object at all**, a genuine upload
failure rather than this bug. The fix bails out before any status write when the
object is absent, so it correctly stays `failed` instead of being papered over.

### Changed

  pre-fix code, where `'failed'` was in the skip-set and a re-drive would have been

## [2026-07-30] — PRISM badge: show the completion date, do NOT publish internal S3 keys (FE #310)

### Fixed — a date that could never render
- The "PRISM ready" tooltip nested its completion date **inside a filename branch** fed by `csv_s3_key`:
  `{filename ? (<div>{filename}{completionDate && …}</div>) : (<div>PRISM result available</div>)}`

### Reversed my own recommendation from #308
- #308 flagged "add `csv_s3_key` to `/v1/prism/requests/me`" as a small backend follow-up. **Bill challenged it and was right.** That change would publish bucket layout and the user id to the browser so a tooltip could display `PRISM,W,B,2026-06-15.csv` — a machine artifact of no use to a reader. The completion date is the thing users actually want and it was already available. Recommendation withdrawn; the endpoint stays as-is.
- Dropped `csv_s3_key` / `pdf_s3_key` from `PrismRequestRow` and `LatestPrismStatus`. **Declaring fields the endpoint never sends is what created the unreachable branch in the first place** — a comment now records why they are deliberately absent. Stale keys cleaned out of the `Home` and `PrismBadge` fixtures too.

### Verified
- T1 now asserts the completion date instead of a filename; new T3 covers the no-date case. Full suite **511 suites / 3894 tests pass**; build clean; **ESLint unchanged** — `Home.test.tsx` reports 8 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` before *and* after, measured by stashing rather than assumed.
- **MERGED + DEPLOYED** (this entry was first written pre-merge): `Deploy to Dev` + `Deploy to Staging-B` both success. Confirmed in the **deployed staging-b chunks** — the badge chunk (`MeridianChat-CS1UhGmM.js`) carries **0** occurrences of `csv_s3_key` and the minified tooltip reads `"PRISM result available"` followed by `c&&…["Completed: ",c]`, i.e. the date on its own with no filename gate; the hook chunk likewise has 0 `csv_s3_key` and reads `data?.rows`.

## [2026-07-30] — Document upload race: files stranded at 'failed', Meridian can't read them

Monorepo PR #725. OPEN — code fix merged/deployed status tracked in the PR.

### Reported
[user M.T.] uploads a PRISM CSV + a job description on staging-b; Meridian keeps
answering that it can't see the documents or that they're still processing. The
same files uploaded by `[email redacted]` three minutes later work.

### Diagnosed — not account-specific, a race [user M.T.] lost and Bill won
- `initiate_upload` emits `document.uploaded` **when it hands out the presigned
  URL** — before the browser has PUT a single byte. EventBridge invokes the
  document-service Lambda on that event, so it races the upload.
- When the Lambda wins: `get_s3_object` → `NoSuchKey` → the broad `except` sets
  `status='failed'` → and because `'failed'` was in the already-processed
  skip-set, the frontend's own `POST /v1/documents/{id}/process` (which fires
  *after* the PUT and would have succeeded) was **discarded**. The file sits in
  S3 intact while its row keeps 0 chunks and a NULL `extracted_text`.
- `retrieve_attached_documents` requires `extracted_text`, so Meridian was
  correctly reporting it couldn't read the document.
- Timeline pulled from CloudWatch + S3, staging-b 2026-07-30: row created
  15:42:36.977 → `NoSuchKey` 15:42:37.684 → **the object lands 15:42:38**. Bill's
  identical upload at 15:45:38 had its PUT land first → `ready`, 14 chunks.
- [user M.T.] had lost the race 3 times across 2 days and 2 of his 4 accounts, then
  succeeded on a third account at 16:05 — the pattern behind "continually".

### Fixed
- `s3_object_exists()` distinguishes "the upload hasn't landed" from "this
  document is unprocessable". Errors other than a missing object still
  propagate, so a permissions fault can't masquerade as a slow upload.
  - Files: `services/document-service/app/storage/s3.py`
- `process_document` bails out **before any status write** when the object is
  absent. Writing `"scanning"` first would have re-armed the guard against the
  very retry it defers to.
- `'failed'` leaves the skip-set so a stranded document recovers on retry.
  `'ready'` stays in it — the 2026-05-13 duplicate-chunk guard is untouched and
  now pinned by a test.
- A mid-pipeline disappearance resets to `'pending'`, not `'failed'`.
  - Files: `services/document-service/app/service.py`
- 12 regression tests; **10 fail against current `development`**, verified by
  reverting the source and re-running. `test_genuine_extraction_failure_still_fails`
  pins that a present-but-corrupt file *does* still latch at `failed` — the fix
  must not swallow real errors.
  - Files: `services/document-service/tests/test_service.py`

### Added
- One-off recovery for the rows already stranded: **19 of the 20 documents at
  `status='failed'` across dev and staging-b have their bytes present in S3**.
  Resets those to `pending` and re-drives processing. The 20th (`my_resume.pdf`,
  dev) has no object — a genuine upload failure, reported and left alone.
  Dry run by default.
  - Files: `scripts/recover_stranded_documents.py`
  - **NOT YET RUN** — blocked pending approval for the DB write.

### Found but NOT fixed (separate issue, flagged not scoped)
- `document_chunks.embedding` is **empty for all 1,858 chunks on staging-b**
  (dev: 1,587 of 3,877, last populated 2026-07-09). `retriever.py` does cosine
  similarity on that column, so corpus-wide semantic retrieval over user
  documents returns nothing on staging-b. The explicit attach path is
  unaffected — it reads `extracted_text` — which is why this did not cause
  [user M.T.]'s symptom and why it has gone unnoticed.

## [2026-07-30] — Meridian chat latency: response budget, progressive delivery, classifier fix

Monorepo PR #724 · Frontend PR #309. Both OPEN, not merged.

### Measured first
- Pulled a full turn trace from live staging-b rather than estimating. `POST /v1/agents/chat/async` → answer took **48.8s**, of which **one non-streaming LLM call was 44.2s (91%)** — `claude-sonnet-4-6`, 12,172 in / 1,610 out, `"stream": false`. Preamble was ~4.3s: two serial haiku calls (891ms intent + 1,393ms agent selection), three OpenAI embedding calls, RAG + memory assembly totalling 38,708 chars for a **78-character** question.
- Two turns fit `answer latency ≈ 4.2s fixed + ~25ms per output token`, which is what makes answer LENGTH the dominant lever.

### Fixed — intent classifier fallback (correctness, not latency)
- `domain = raw if raw in (...) else "coaching"` discarded the keyword vote and returned a **hardcoded literal** on any malformed reply; only an *exception* reached the keyword fallback. Live traffic showed the classifier answering the user's question conversationally and being truncated at `max_tokens=20`, so those turns routed to coaching regardless of keyword scores. Agent selection was effectively being made by a default.
- Now: lenient label parse (accepts `Domain: business.`, rejects a reply echoing all four), then the keyword pick. Decision path logged as `source=` so malformed verdicts are countable in CloudWatch. The call also delimits the message and cues `Domain:` so the model classifies instead of answering.
  - Files: `services/agent-engine/app/agents/meridian.py`

### Added — conversational response budget
- `chat_response_max_tokens` (900) seeded via `setdefault` at the top of `respond()`/`route()`, plus a constant brevity directive on the **static** system block. The directive is the real lever — a bare token cap truncates mid-sentence rather than producing a shorter answer.
- Long-form callers (Honor evaluation narration, document generation) raise `max_output_tokens` themselves and are skipped by both mechanisms. Aura now honours the budget the way Nova already did.
- The directive is a constant, so it does not disturb the Anthropic cache prefix (cf. the 2026-06-18 cache investigation, where a per-turn injection into `messages[0]` silently zeroed `cache_read`).
  - Files: `app/config.py`, `app/agents/base_agent.py`, `app/agents/meridian.py`, `app/agents/coaching/prism_agent.py`

### Added — progressive delivery over the existing 2s poll
- `chat_jobs.content` already accepted writes on a non-terminal row and the frontend already fetched `job.content` on every poll — the only missing piece was anything producing partial text.
- New `app/agents/partial_dispatch.py` is a drop-in for `agent.process()`: **no sink installed** → calls `process()`, byte-identical to before; **sink installed** → accumulates `agent.stream()` and flushes the answer-so-far on a ~1s throttle. Streamed usage/model is folded back from the provider's `LAST_STREAM_*` ContextVars so cost tracking does not under-report, and `respond()` skips its observability row when `stream()` already wrote one.
- **Applied only at unambiguously single-agent dispatch sites** (Meridian sticky + timeout fallback; the `single_agent_direct` branch in all four orchestrators). `DAGExecutor` and `run_multi_domain` still call `agent.process()` directly, so multi-agent planning behaviour is untouched.
- Frontend: new pure helper `src/lib/chat/applyPartial.ts` folds the partial into the newest in-flight bubble, returning the SAME array reference when nothing changed so an unchanged poll costs no re-render. `MeridianChat` wires `onJobUpdate` — the hook already fired it on every poll and nothing consumed it.
  - Files: `app/main.py`, `app/agents/orchestrators/*.py`, `src/lib/chat/applyPartial.ts`, `src/pages/user/MeridianChat.tsx`

### Verified against a measured baseline
- Agent-engine suite run **3×**. Baseline with changes stashed at the same commit: **167 failed / 3836 passed**. With changes: **167 failed / 3868 passed**, failure sets byte-identical (`comm -13` empty). +32 new backend tests, +7 frontend.
- One flake seen once in `test_chat_jobs.py::test_post_async_then_poll_to_completion`; did not reproduce across two further full runs and sits outside the diff's blast radius.
- Frontend: 510 suites / 3886 tests pass, clean `npm run build`, eslint 0 errors with the 7 `exhaustive-deps` warnings proven pre-existing by stashing and re-linting.
- The three new/updated backend test files were added to `pr-validation.yml`'s agent-engine allowlist — without that they would gate nothing.

### Not done (deliberately)
- Prompt-caching the 30,491-char attached document (it sits in the dynamic block after the cache breakpoint by design) — buys ~2s and a large share of the token bill, but is the fiddliest of the four and was scoped out.
- SSE streaming stays OFF. Progressive delivery over polling gets most of the perceived win without the API Gateway 30s-cap exposure.
- Two broken tables on staging-b remain unfixed: `response_decision_rules` does not exist, and the RLHF `ModelRouter` DynamoDB table is not found. Neither causes the latency; both mean a feature believed on is off.

## [2026-07-30] — PRISM questionnaire link now recoverable + `/requests/me` contract fixed (FE #308)

### Added — the link survives a reload
- **`ActivePrismRequestCard`** renders one card per still-open questionnaire type, above the request form on **both** `/prism-assessment` pages (V1 + V2): type label, requested date, the URL, **Open Questionnaire** and **Copy link**.
- Why it was needed: the link was shown **exactly once**, in the submit success card, and was gone on reload — even though both ActionURLs are persisted on `prism_requests` and returned by `GET /v1/prism/requests/me`. Nothing rendered them, so a user who closed the tab had no route back to their own survey. Dev and staging-b have each been sitting on a **week-old pending row in exactly that state**.
- Reads `action_url_1 || action_url_2`, because PRISM leaves ActionURL1 empty for a freshly created candidate and puts the questionnaire link in ActionURL2.
- New hook `useActivePrismRequests()` wraps `useMyPrismRequests()` — no extra network call.

### Changed — removed a promise the product may not keep
- The request form claimed *"PRISM will send questionnaire access to this email"*. **We make no such call** — there is no SES send anywhere in `prism_request.py` — and whether PRISM emails the candidate is their configuration, unverified by us. It had users waiting for mail that may never arrive instead of using the link on screen. Replaced with what we can stand behind.

### Fixed — `GET /v1/prism/requests/me` contract mismatch (found while building the above)
| | Backend `RequestListResponse`/`RequestRow` | FE type (before) |
|---|---|---|
| list key | `rows` | `items` ❌ |
| row id | `id` | `request_id` ❌ |
| `action_url_2` | returned | **absent** ❌ |
| `csv_s3_key`, `pdf_s3_key`, `quest_status_desc`, `created_at`, `updated_at` | not returned | required ❌ |
- Consequence: `useLatestPrismStatus` read `q.data?.items`, always got `[]`, and **`PrismBadge`'s "PRISM ready" could never render** — a silent dead feature. The type also omitted `action_url_2`, so the new card could not have worked without this fix.
- **The existing test fixture encoded the same wrong shape**, which is exactly why the mismatch survived. Fixed the types, the hook, and the fixture.
- **Knock-on, deliberate:** PrismBadge will now render when `ingest_status === 'done'`. Its tooltip filename comes from `csv_s3_key`, which this endpoint does not return, so it falls back to the no-filename branch — still strictly better than a badge that never appeared. Adding `csv_s3_key` to the endpoint is a backend change, out of scope.

### Verified
- 5 new card tests (hidden while loading, hidden when none open, link surfaced with correct `href`/`target`, one card per concurrent type, explanatory fallback when PRISM has issued no link) + 2 new hook tests (`rows` key; open-only rows with URL1→URL2 resolution).
- Full suite **510 suites / 3886 tests pass**; `npm run build` clean; ESLint clean on all 7 changed files.

The staging-b build (rebuilt against `.env.staging-b`) never set it, so the Studio was dark there even though the backend (growth-service + agent-engine dossier + PRISM read-model) is promoted and demo data is seeded on staging-b.

### Changed (frontend repo `inspire-genius-frontend`, PR #305)
- `.env.staging-b`: `VITE_FEATURE_TEAM_DEVELOPMENT=true` (the staging-b build uses this as its base `.env`), alongside the other staging-b feature flags.
- `.github/workflows/ci-deploy.yml`: updated the dev build-step comment (flag no longer dev-only).

### Diagnosis (definitive, from live bundles)
- Both dev + staging-b were on the same git build but different bundles (different `.env`). Grepping the deployed JS: the **dev** bundle contained the "Team Development" nav (flag on → Studio live); the **staging-b** bundle did NOT (flag off → old interface). The Studio surfaces already consume the real `growthService` (`/v1/growth`) — no mock data — so the only gap was the build flag.

### Verified (live)
- FE PR #305 merged → ci-deploy rebuilt + deployed both envs. staging-b now serves version `8c6e7cb` with the "Team Development" nav present in the bundle (was absent); dev unchanged (no regression). Backend confirmed earlier: staging-b roster query returns the 6 seeded members by name; member dossier computes real PRISM (assessment-derived) + seeded goals. So the Studio is live + wired to real data on staging-b (browser access via magic-link/Cognito — email-only magic-auth is off there per #717).

## [2026-07-30] — Lumen coaching answers on the page, with print + Word/PDF export

Lumen **Personal coaching** now answers **on the page** instead of navigating away to the Meridian chat surface. Answers accumulate, so a run of questions reads as one session, and each answer can be **copied, printed, or exported to Word or PDF** — the same per-turn controls Meridian chat has.

### Why the old behaviour was wrong
Asking a question threw the person out of Lumen and discarded the context they had just assembled with the source checkboxes. The answer arrived somewhere that no longer knew why it had been asked.

### Added
- `src/pages/lumen/CoachingAnswers.tsx` — the response window. Renders through `AssistantMarkdown` (coaching answers are mostly headings and lists; flattening them to one grey paragraph is what makes an inline answer feel worse than the chat). Per-answer **Copy / Print / Export ▾ (Word, PDF)**.
- `src/hooks/lumen/useCoachAnswer.ts` — wraps the Meridian async-job path into ask → answer. One session id per page mount, so successive questions are one conversation.
- `src/lib/exportTranscript/printTurn.ts` — printing, sharing `buildTurnHtml` with `exportTurn`.

### Changed
- `src/pages/lumen/CoachingPage.tsx` — **"Answer it here"** is now the primary action; **"Open in Meridian"** remains as secondary for anyone who wants to keep talking rather than read one answer. Picking a question from the dropdown answers it inline.

### How it works — and what it deliberately does NOT do
Inline answers go through the **ordinary async-job path** (`POST /v1/agents/chat/async` → poll `GET /v1/agents/chat/jobs/{id}`):

- **Meridian is not bypassed.** She still classifies and routes to whichever specialist the question needs.
- **No backend change, so no promote is needed.** Job Fit could answer inline (#306) because it already had `explain-fit`; Lumen has no equivalent, and a *synchronous* LLM route would sit behind API Gateway's hard 30s cap. The async path is the one built for this.
- **The poll is the delivery mechanism** — the `job_complete` WS push is not reachable through the production ws-proxy — so the hook opens no socket at all.

### Decisions worth keeping
- **Print and Export share one document builder.** The printout, the `.doc` and the PDF are the same artefact rather than three near-misses; a test pins the printed input as deep-equal to the exported one.
- **The scope line is not part of the question.** `Draw on my PRISM scores…` is an instruction to the coach — it goes into the prompt but is kept out of the answer heading and the exported file, which read as the question actually asked. The exported document leads with the question, because a download read a week later has none of the on-screen context.
- **`printTurn` uses an off-screen iframe, not `window.open`** — a popup blocker swallows the latter silently, leaving no error to explain the nothing that happened.
- **One job at a time**; overlapping asks would land out of order. A start-job failure clears the pending state, since `onJobSettled` never fires for a job that was never accepted and the spinner would otherwise run forever.

### Verified against dev before merging, not asserted
Exercised the real path with a real token: `POST /v1/agents/chat/async` → **202**, poll → running → **complete in ~9s**, and `metadata.contributing_agents` came back as **`['Summit']`** — Meridian routed a goal question to the goal agent, which is the routing this design depends on.

### Tests
97 passing across `pages/lumen/`, `hooks/lumen/` and `lib/exportTranscript/`. Three existing tests asserted the old navigate-away behaviour and were **rewritten to express the new intent** rather than deleted.

Deliberately stayed off `SelfPortrait.tsx`, `types/lumen.ts` and `useSelfPortrait.ts` — FE #312 was open on those files from another terminal, and merged mid-build. Re-checked afterwards: **no conflict**, merges clean.

### Known duplication — Lumen now has two export document builders
FE #312 landed `src/lib/lumen/portraitReport.ts` (Self-Portrait report) at almost the same time. It shares the *plumbing* — `renderHtmlToPdf` and `downloadBlob` from `exportTranscript` — but has its own HTML builder and its own small markdown→HTML converter, because a portrait report (headline, instruments, coverage, disclaimer, Q&A) is a genuinely different document shape from a single turn. This work reuses `buildTurnHtml` instead, because a coaching answer *is* a turn — which is also what was asked for ("like the one in chat with Meridian").

So the duplication is limited to two small markdown converters, and is **accepted for now** rather than resolved by refactoring another terminal's freshly-merged code. Per the standing rule, extract on the **third** occurrence or the first behavioural drift between them.

**PR:** FE #313. Frontend-only, so it reaches **dev and staging-B** on merge without a backend promote.

## [2026-07-29] — LOE assessment: Meridian "Projects" tile persistence (no code change)

### Assessed — decision input, nothing shipped
- Question: human + CC level of effort to give the Meridian header's **Projects** tile a real backend. It is currently a `localStorage`-only list (`meridian:projects:v2`), so projects do not follow a user across devices or survive a cache clear. Nobody has asked for it; raised proactively after FE #301.

### The finding that sets the price
- **There is no `conversations` table.** On `origin/development`, `GET /v1/agents/conversations` derives the list with `GROUP BY session_id` over `chat_messages`, and a conversation's title is a sentinel row (`__CONV_TITLE__:`) inside the message stream. So there is nothing for a `project_id` to hang off — which is what separates "persist the list" from "projects that group chats" by roughly an order of magnitude.

### Estimates (CC sessions and human hours are NOT converted into each other)
- **Scope A — parity (persist the list, no behaviour change): CC 2–3 · Human 2–3 h · Confidence A.**
  Anchored to a measured near-exact analogue, Lumen saved-prompts: backend `073cef07` = 669 insertions / 6 files (migration 67 L, model +51, routes +96, tool module 186 L, tests 218 L, inline-SQL mirror 51 L); frontend `97599c2` = 417 insertions / 8 files (hook 55 L, service 55 L, types +23, wiring +134, tests +99). The two commits landed **8m36s apart** inside the 4h42m block that produced 5 BE + 5 FE PRs. Projects is simpler — no `use_count` promotion or reuse ordering. Next migration is **023**. Human time is almost entirely non-delegable: review, the **manual** migration on dev and again on staging-b (~0.5 h per env), and browser verification.
- **Scope B1 — projects that group conversations, via a `session_id` join table: CC 4–6 · Human 5–8 h · Confidence B.** The join table is not the risk; every list query (Active / History / Last 5) needs a project filter, which means editing the `GROUP BY` query with its hand-written correlated subqueries and its "search mode loads up to 10,000 rows" fallback — the most load-bearing query in the chat surface. Plus orphan handling, since sessions are derived from messages that can age out.
- **Scope B2 — promote conversations to a first-class table** (backfill, dual-write, retire the title sentinel): **CC 10–15 · Human 12–20 h · Confidence C** — no comparable in this repo, so ±100% until spiked. A refactor of chat persistence, not a feature.
- **Scope C — delete the tile: CC <1 · Human 0.25 h · Confidence A.** ~95 lines of frontend, no backend, no migration.

### Overheads priced in (both easy to forget)
- A new `tests/…/test_projects.py` **will not run in any gating job** unless its filename is added to the hardcoded 13-name allowlist at `.github/workflows/pr-validation.yml:222`.
- The frontend CI coverage gate is a **global 55%** with roughly 5 points of headroom.

### Recommendation
- **Do not build Scope A.** Persisting the list makes the feature look real while the control still does nothing — 2–3 sessions to make a dead control durable. Either take Scope C now, or B1 when grouped chats are actually asked for.

## [2026-07-29] — PRISM request 500: one-survey-per-user-for-life constraint (BE #720, NOT yet deployed)

### The defect — surfaced only once the FE started submitting
- **`POST /v1/prism/requests` returned 500 on staging-b.** The PRISM call had **succeeded**: `httpx` logged `POST …/api.svc/CreateCandidate "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"` with a live ActionURL2, and then **our own INSERT** raised `asyncpg.UniqueViolationError` on `uq_prism_requests_user_external_ident`.
- **Root cause:** the constraint was `UNIQUE (user_id, external_ident)` and the route always sets `external_ident = str(user_id)` — collapsing to **one PRISM request per user, for life**. A second questionnaire was impossible, not even a different **type** (Bill requested QTypeID 1 / Professional while holding an existing row).
- **The 24h idempotency pre-check did not rescue it** — it only matched rows with `completed_at IS NULL`, so a completed or stale row fell straight through into a doomed insert.
- **Worse than a rejected request:** PRISM is called **before** the insert, so each attempt created a **real candidate** — burning licence quota — and then discarded the questionnaire link with a 500.
- **Not a regression from #300/#302.** This backend defect was *unreachable* until the FE started submitting, which is precisely why `prism_requests` was 0 rows in both envs. The FE fix exposed it.

### Fixed (BE PR #720 — open, CI green, NOT merged/deployed)
- **Constraint → `UNIQUE (user_id, external_ident, qtype_id)`** — migration `023_prism_requests_unique_per_qtype.py` + migration-runner mirror `prism_requests_unique_per_qtype.sql`. A user may hold several concurrent surveys of different types.
- **Idempotency pre-check scoped per `qtype_id`**, so an in-flight Foundation request no longer suppresses a Professional one. Re-requesting the *same* type stays guarded by the 24h window — policy in the route, not in a constraint that can only fail *after* the third-party call.
- **INSERT wrapped in `except IntegrityError`** → refresh the existing row onto the newly-issued link and reopen its lifecycle. Once PRISM has created the candidate, a DB conflict must never surface as a 500.
- **Unpersistable-link logging.** Where the fallback must still re-raise, the issued ActionURLs are logged at ERROR first — that is how tonight's live link was recovered from CloudWatch, and it turns a burnt licence seat into a recoverable incident.
- Checked the poller before widening the key: it `select()`s a **list** and loops per row, so multiple rows sharing an `external_ident` are safe.
- Files: `services/agent-engine/app/models/prism_request.py`, `app/routes/prism_request.py`, `alembic/versions/023_*`, `services/migration-runner/migrations/prism_requests_unique_per_qtype.sql`, + 2 test files

### The migration is a HARD dependency — verified, not assumed
- Merging the code alone does **not** fix it. Traced the fallback against an unmigrated DB: with the legacy key, a *different* qtype raises `IntegrityError`, the handler finds **no same-qtype row** to refresh, and re-raises → still a 500. Constraint first, then code.

### Verified
- 3 new tests (second qtype → second row + 2 PRISM calls; same qtype after completion → 200 with fresh link, row reused, not 500; schema allows differing qtype **and** asserts the old constraint is gone rather than merely supplemented). Both changed test files are in the `pr-validation.yml` agent-engine allowlist, so they genuinely gate.
- Full agent-engine suite **167 failed / 3821 passed** vs baseline **167 failed / 3818 passed** — identical failure count, +3 from these tests. The 167 are pre-existing local env failures (no OpenAI key / AWS creds), confirmed by re-running with the change stashed rather than assumed.

### BLOCKED — awaiting Bill
- **Dev Aurora migration not applied.** `ig-dev-migration-runner` invoke was refused by the safety classifier (DDL). Probe confirmed dev still carries `uq_prism_requests_user_external_ident UNIQUE (user_id, external_ident)`.
- **staging-b untouched** — its migration + agent-engine promote remain always-confirm.

## [2026-07-29] — Growth roster resolves member NAMES via direct public.team_members read (PR #719, LIVE dev + staging-b)

Fixed the Team Development roster showing member IDs instead of names (surfaced by the staging-b Summit seed).

### Fixed
- `growth-service list_roster` sourced its team from `client.get_team()`, which calls `settings.agent_engine_url + /api/manager/team` — but `/api/manager/team` is a **dashboard-service** route the agent-engine doesn't serve, so it 404'd, the exception was swallowed, and the roster fell back to persisted dossiers whose `member.name` is the raw `member_id`. (Even reaching dashboard, it gates on role `manager`; magic-auth mints `role:user`.)
  - Now reads dashboard-service's `public.team_members` **directly** over the shared Aurora/RDS-Proxy connection (sanctioned cross-schema read) — it carries the real name/email/prism_color, no HTTP hop, no manager-role token. New `_fetch_team_members()`; schema-qualified so `search_path`-independent; any error → `[]` so the persisted-dossier + legacy `get_team` fallbacks still run.
  - Files: `services/growth-service/app/service.py`, tests `services/growth-service/tests/test_team_members_read.py` (48 growth tests pass).

### Verified
- **Dev E2E** (magic-auth on `[api-id]`): seeded one dev `team_members` row (willb77→[user D.R.]) → `GET /v1/growth/roster` returns **`name":"[user D.R.]"`** (team-backed member resolves the real name; dossier-only members correctly still show IDs). Dev verify row removed after.
- **staging-b** (promoted via tag `release-stable-2026-07-28-roster-names`, delta = #719 only, no migrations; growth Lambda redeployed 04:06 UTC): the exact query the fix runs returns all 6 seeded names ([user J.B.], [user J.B.]., [user Li.B.], Naomi Boyer, [user R.K.B.], Rebekah Hartberger) — all 6 are `team_members`-backed so the roster resolves them by name. (magic-auth is now off on staging-b per #717, so the full API E2E was done on dev; the deployed code + data path are confirmed on staging-b.)

## [2026-07-28] — PRISM "Request Assessment" submit was a no-op — wired to the survey-request API

### Fixed
- **`/prism-assessment` could not request a PRISM report from PRISM UK — the submit button did nothing at all.** Reported from staging-b. `PrismInitiateForm` was built as a design-time harness with an optional `onSubmit` prop carrying the real API call; both `PrismAssessment.tsx:96` and `PrismAssessmentV2.tsx:103` render it as `<PrismInitiateForm disabled={...} />` — **no `onSubmit`**. The handler therefore ended at `onSubmitProp?.(values, apiPayload)` against `undefined`: zod validated, a payload object was built, and it was discarded. No network request, no toast, no error, no visible change. FE PR #300.
  - Confirmed in the **deployed staging-b bundle**, not just source: page chunks passed a single prop (`I,{disabled:!!n}` / `A,{disabled:!!m}`) and the minified handler terminated at `j?.(s,a)`. The harness tell (`staging.prismbrainmapping.com/questionnaire/demo`) was present in the shipped chunk.
  - `PrismInitiateForm` now calls `useRequestPrismSurvey()` itself, mapping `questionnaireTypeId → qtype_id`, `languageId → lang_id`, `gender === 'male' → gender` (PRISM convention: true = male), `isGift → isGift` (backend aliases `is_gift`).
  - `showPayloadPreview` is now the explicit **harness switch** (preserves preview-only, no-network behaviour for `/dev/prism-test-harness`); `onSubmit` is demoted to an observer fired *alongside* the real call rather than replacing it.
  - Success state gated on a new `submitted` flag instead of `questionnaireUrl` being truthy — a request succeeding without an `action_url_1` previously fell through to the form and reproduced the very "nothing happens" symptom being fixed.
  - Files: `src/components/prism/PrismInitiateForm.tsx`, `src/services/prism/prism.ts` (`PrismSurveyRequestPayload` + `lang_id`/`gender`/`isGift`), `src/components/prism/__tests__/PrismInitiateForm.test.tsx`

### The second half of the defect — wrong route family
- The form was written against endpoints that **were never built**: probing staging-b returned **404** for `POST /v1/prism/initiate`, `GET /v1/prism/history/{userId}`, `/status/{id}`, `/report/{id}`. Only `POST /v1/prism/requests` (401 — exists, auth-gated), `/requests/me`, `/check-customer` and `/poll/run` are live.
- Cause of the split: `prism_request.py` mounts at **`/v1/prism`**, while `prism.py` (list/get + 410-deprecated mutations) mounts at **`/v1/agents/prism`** — a different prefix. `prism.service.ts` targets the former path with the latter's assumptions.
- The working surface (`RequestPrismDialog` → `useRequestPrismSurvey` → `POST /v1/prism/requests`, reached from the Home "Take PRISM Assessment" tile and the chat PrismBadge) was already correct and is untouched.

### Deliberately unchanged
- **Assessment History and Import Existing Report on that page stay inert.** `usePrismHistory` is already knowingly disabled (`enabled: false` default, backlog #10.U) because its endpoint was never built — so it is not a live 404, and repointing it at `GET /v1/prism/requests/me` is a separate change. Kept out to hold this PR to the submit path.
- `reference` and `createUser` remain form-only — backend `CreateRequestBody` has no matching fields. Still shown in the harness payload preview.

### Verified
- 5 new wiring tests (payload mapping, link render, no-link fallback, failure path, harness-mode-stays-offline); `PrismInitiateForm.test.tsx` 11/11.
- `npm run test:ci` — **502 suites / 3817 tests pass**, no regressions. `npm run build` clean. ESLint clean on all 3 changed files (repo-wide baseline of 795 pre-existing errors untouched).
- Verified in the **rebuilt** bundle: the form chunk now imports `usePrismRequest-*.js` (which carries `/v1/prism/requests`) and the submit path compiles to `await b.mutateAsync({forename...})` — neither was present before.
